12545.summary: God would do all the work to bring Israel into the land if they only trusted Him, a picture of salvation as a free gift without our works.

12549.title: The twelve spies a picture of the twelve apostles
12549.summary: The twelve spies bringing first ripe grapes picture the apostles sent two by two to gather the firstfruits, and soul winners today must be of good courage before the harvest.

12553.title: God hates them that sow discord
12553.summary: God hates those who sow discord and spread a bad report in the church, and believers should rebuke them and be like Caleb, a blessing who builds up.

12554.title: Forty years from the cross to 70 AD
12554.summary: The generation that died in the wilderness pictures the unbelieving Jews cut off, forty years from the crucifixion to Jerusalem's fall in 70 AD.

12562.title: Ordinances a memorial of Christ
12562.summary: The offerings pictured Christ as the Lord's supper memorializes Him, ordinances having no power themselves, and the stranger always had the same salvation by faith.

12571.title: Korah's rebellion: unbelief and reprobation
12571.summary: Korah and the rebels were destroyed and sent to hell for unbelief and rebellion against the man of God, showing God cut off Israelites from His promises.

12573.title: Korah's company the first ecumenical council
12573.summary: Korah's rebellion is like Rome's councils, adding the traditions of men such as baptismal regeneration, infant baptism and idols to God's word.

12581.theme: Christ our King and High Priest
12581.title: Aaron's rod that budded
12581.summary: Aaron's dead rod that budded pictures Christ, the risen Branch and our High Priest, whom men resent and rebel against today.

12599.theme: Christ our King and High Priest
12599.title: The Levites' portion and Christ our High Priest
12599.summary: The Levitical covenant pictures Christ our only High Priest, which Jews no longer have, and the Levites' lack of land pictures our separation from this world.

12601.title: The red heifer fulfilled in Christ
12601.summary: The red heifer burned with cedar, hyssop and scarlet pictures Christ's sacrifice, not a prophecy needed for a third temple.

12602.theme: Christ our King and High Priest
12602.title: The covenant of salt
12602.summary: The covenant of salt given to Aaron's priesthood and David's kingdom is fulfilled in Christ, and believers are the salt that preserves the world.

12619.title: Speak to the rock
12619.summary: Speaking to the rock pictures calling upon Christ for living water, and Moses lost the promised land by striking it in disobedience.

12621.title: Obedience brings victory, disobedience fear
12621.summary: Obedience brought Israel water and victory while disobedience sent them away in fear, as backsliding Christians retreat until they humbly return to a forgiving God.

12636.title: The brazen serpent lifted up
12636.summary: When Israel despised the manna God sent serpents, and the brazen serpent lifted up pictures Christ, that whosoever looks to Him should live.

12637.title: Beware extrabiblical books
12637.summary: Books lost to us were not needed, and seeking apocrypha and forgeries like Enoch snares believers, so read the Bible many times before histories.

12638.title: Nehushtan: no license for idolatry
12638.summary: The brazen serpent was a picture of Christ, not an object of worship, and Hezekiah destroyed it when Israel burned incense to it, as crucifixes are worshipped today.

12681.theme: The church is the Israel of God
12681.title: Inheritance by law, blessing by election
12681.summary: Scripture throughout shows earthly inheritance by law but spiritual blessing by election, picturing the Gentiles adopted in Christ over Abraham's children after the flesh.

12710.title: Spoil purified by fire and our works tried
12710.summary: The spoil passed through fire pictures our works tried by fire, the treasure we lay up in heaven and the crowns cast at Christ's feet.

12739.theme: The church is the Israel of God
12739.title: The land given by the election of grace
12739.summary: Israel's inheritance was always conditional and by God's election of grace, and Numbers shows He casts off any branches into the fire.

12748.title: Blood pollutes the land: the cities of refuge
12748.summary: Bloodshed pollutes the land and brought judgment on Canaan and then Israel, so God's law of refuge cities minimized bloodshed.

12773.title: Divisions and pride in Corinth
12773.summary: Paul rebukes the divisions in Corinth, for God uses the weak and foolish so that no flesh glories and the church is of one mind in Christ.

12781.title: The things of God are spiritually discerned
12781.summary: Understanding of the things of God is a gift of the Spirit through the word, so the natural man who seeks worldly wisdom finds them foolishness.

12782.title: Spiritual blindness and willingness to receive
12782.summary: Heretics who seek validation rather than truth are spiritually blind, while saved people misled can be corrected by scripture if willing.

12790.title: Abstain for the weaker brother's sake
12790.summary: Our sanctification is for others, so we abstain even from lawful things if they lead a weaker brother to sin or reject Christ.

12798.title: Baptized by one Spirit into one body
12798.summary: 1 Corinthians 12 calls the proud Corinthians to humility as one body under Christ, not to make the gifts evidence of salvation as Pentecostals do.

12799.title: The gifts of wisdom and knowledge
12799.summary: The manifestation of the Spirit is given to profit others, and wisdom and knowledge come by studying the word to serve the brethren, not to be puffed up.

12817.title: The more excellent way is the heart
12817.summary: The lists of gifts in Romans 12 and 1 Corinthians 12 are about the hearts of believers toward the gifts, that all work as one body under Christ.

12818.title: Simon the sorcerer coveting the gift
12818.summary: Simon coveted the apostles' power and was rebuked, showing that envy, strife and pride have no part in the gifts God gives.

12819.title: Pride turns the gifts into doctrine
12819.summary: False churches made the list of gifts primary doctrine out of pride and covetousness, and gifted men can use knowledge, governance or preaching for their own prominence.

12820.title: False prophets claiming God told me
12820.summary: The less gifted who covet prominence turn to obscure doctrines and claimed visions and revelations, attention-seeking lies that lead others astray.

12821.title: Faith healers are reprobate
12821.summary: God still heals through prayer, but faith healers who fake miracles for money blaspheme the Holy Ghost and bring a bad report on God's power.

12827.title: Speaking in tongues was known languages
12827.summary: Tongues at Pentecost were real foreign languages for spreading the gospel, and Paul's tongues of angels is a hypothetical, not a doctrine.

12828.title: Pentecostal tongues are faked babbling
12828.summary: Pentecostal tongue speaking is pride-driven faked babbling that edifies no one, against what Paul teaches.

12829.title: Known by their fruits: Pentecostal delusion
12829.summary: The saved can be corrected by scripture, but Pentecostals and Charismatics double down, hold works salvation and other heresies, and are known by their fruits.

12832.title: Tongues are for a sign to unbelievers
12832.summary: Tongues were a sign to unbelievers that they might hear the gospel, showing God's word keeps its power in every language, and gifts are to be used decently with charity.

12846.title: The gift of helps
12846.summary: The gift of helps or ministry is serving one another as members of one body, as Paul praised his fellow laborers in Romans 16.

12848.title: Pure religion: visit the fatherless and widows
12848.summary: Christ's reading of Isaiah is our mission statement, so true religion serves the poor, the brokenhearted and the needy in deed, not words only.

12849.title: Seek to be a help in the church
12849.summary: Helping is the most neglected gift, so we should come to church looking to be a blessing and serve with cheer.

12858.title: Little ones with no knowledge of good and evil
12858.summary: Deuteronomy 1 shows an age of accountability, children being innocent without the law, against the original sin teaching behind infant baptism.

12865.title: Promises to Lot and Esau, and nations judged
12865.summary: God gave land to Lot and Esau too, yet destroyed those nations for wickedness, so modern Jews have no claim, for God gives and takes away the bounds of nations.

12868.title: Faith in the face of giants
12868.summary: Like Caleb, faith acts on belief rather than fear, and God delivers through tribulation and builds our faith as we trust Him.

12880.title: Not forcing the issue: waiting on God
12880.summary: Israel was routed when they fought without God but their children won easily on His schedule, teaching faith, patience and meekness rather than taking matters into our own hands.

12896.title: Ye shall not add unto the word
12896.summary: God's statutes are for our good, and the command not to add to or diminish His word condemns the false versions that do so today.

12898.title: No similitude: flee idols
12898.summary: God showed no form at Horeb, so any image or veneration in worship is idolatry, which Rome hides by removing the second commandment.

12900.title: If my people humble themselves
12900.summary: God offers nations under judgment a way back, as with Nineveh, if they turn from idols and wickedness and seek Him.

12902.theme: Every word of God is pure
12902.title: One consistent voice in all of scripture
12902.summary: He notes that Moses, the prophets, the apostles and Christ all speak with one clear voice because all scripture is given by the same Spirit, not the works of men.

12910.title: The second commandment against Rome's idols
12910.summary: He teaches that bowing, praying, lighting candles and holding vigils before idols and icons in the Roman church is worship and blasphemy forbidden by the second commandment.

12911.title: The Sabbath a picture of rest in Christ
12911.summary: He teaches that the Sabbath pictures our rest in Jesus, that we contribute no works to salvation, and that those who add works damn themselves.

12912.title: Remember thou wast a servant in Egypt
12912.summary: Remembering we were servants to sin freed only by grace, believers should show the same mercy to others, even strangers, that they may come to Christ.

12914.title: The commandments are still in force
12914.summary: He refutes professing Christians who use the end of ceremonial laws to excuse sodomy and adultery, teaching that God's moral commandments still stand.

12923.title: An inheritance we did not build
12923.summary: Like Israel given cities and wells they did not build, believers receive an incorruptible heavenly inheritance in Christ as a gift, to be remembered with humility.

12974.title: Not for thy righteousness
12974.summary: As God gave Israel the land not for their righteousness, we receive the kingdom only by Christ's imputed righteousness, so we must not boast against others (Romans 11).

13009.title: Love God and thy neighbour, for thy good
13009.summary: He teaches the God of the Old Testament is the same as the New, that His commandments were always for our good, and that making them a means of salvation breeds selfishness.

13023.title: Ye shall not do so unto the Lord
13023.summary: God forbade Israel to worship Him with the pagans' images and high places, which he says plainly repudiates Catholic use of icons and idols.

13024.theme: Every word of God is pure
13024.title: Add not to the word nor diminish
13024.summary: He teaches that the word of God is the only authority, given plainly and preserved so even a babe in Christ can understand it, unlike mystery religions and gnosticism.

13026.title: Every man right in his own eyes
13026.summary: He teaches that the blessings of liberty come from a people who believe and obey God, not from every man doing what is right in his own eyes as libertine conservatives do.

13027.title: God's law is not libertarian
13027.summary: Against internet theologians who call Israel's law libertarian, he teaches God ordains government for judgment and the godlier a people, the freer they are.

13043.title: Everything is downstream from God
13043.summary: He teaches that free speech and gun rights only work among a godly people, because God judges individuals by grace and faith but nations by their works.

13048.title: His commandments come with a promise
13048.summary: He teaches that God forgives His children in Christ and gives commandments only so that it be well with us, wanting to bless us and train us as princes of His Kingdom.

13063.title: Clean and unclean meats done away in Christ
13063.summary: He teaches the dietary laws were carnal ordinances picturing separation from the Gentiles until the reformation in Christ, and the peculiar people now are those cleansed by His blood.

13070.title: Release of debts a picture of salvation
13070.summary: The release of servants and debts in the seventh year pictures salvation in Christ, so we should forgive debts as God forgave ours and send others away blessed.

13079.title: The three feasts pictured Jesus
13079.summary: He teaches the pilgrimage feasts picture Jesus and set up His return to Jerusalem at Passover and the gathering at Pentecost, as His children will be gathered at His return.

13080.title: Every man shall give as he is able
13080.summary: Blessed by God, believers give back as they are able in two main ways, winning souls and executing right judgment for the fatherless and widow.

13081.title: God hates your images
13081.summary: He teaches God hates any image set up for worship, with no allowance for intention or veneration, and that Catholic and Orthodox icons bring His judgment.

13086.title: Any host of heaven, including the saints
13086.summary: He teaches the ban on worshipping any host of heaven includes the Catholic saints, and that a blemished sacrifice pictures halfway believers who never truly trust Christ.

13087.title: God's commands for the king
13087.summary: From the law of the king he teaches a ruler must be a brother, not multiply horses, wives or riches, since empire built on man's might is the seed of a nation's fall.

13088.title: A copy of the law for kings and heirs
13088.summary: As kings were to copy and read the law, believers who will reign with Christ must learn scripture to judge rightly, turning neither to the political left nor right but to God's way.

13092.title: Divination and Moloch an abomination
13092.summary: He teaches that child sacrifice like abortion, divination, astrology and mediums are abominations, practitioners being both frauds and conduits for Satan.

13093.title: The Prophet like unto Moses
13093.summary: Moses foretold Christ the Prophet, and gave the test for false prophets that Jesus repeated: ye shall know them by their fruits.

13094.title: No dispensation, no repeal
13094.summary: He teaches God's civil laws still stand for nations, the law being a schoolmaster to bring men to Christ, because God and His judgment on the wicked do not change.

13101.title: Put away the guilt of innocent blood
13101.summary: He teaches that God's law is founded on justice and avoiding innocent blood, so opposing the death penalty pities murderers and keeps the guilt on the nation.

13108.title: The Lord goeth with you to fight
13108.summary: As God promised to fight Israel's battles against greater armies, the God who delivered us from sin and hell will deliver us in life's smaller battles.

13109.title: Proclaim peace, then fight
13109.summary: He teaches godly people should first offer peace to enemies as a mercy and a show of strength, knowing our victory is already won in Christ.

13117.title: Regulating polygamy is not condoning it
13117.summary: He teaches the firstborn law for a man with two wives regulates sin but does not approve polygamy, and tentatively sees Christ as the firstborn heir.

13118.title: The stubborn and rebellious son
13118.summary: He teaches the law of the rebellious son was a deterrent making it rare, kinder than raising a generation of undisciplined, reprobate children.

13138.title: Help thy neighbour in his need
13138.summary: The laws on lost property and helping a neighbour in a bind are simply love thy neighbour, doing to others as we would have done to us.

13139.title: Man and woman shall not swap garments
13139.summary: He teaches the command against cross-dressing is about modesty and avoiding gender confusion, and that the unisex agenda led to the transgender crisis.

13144.title: The law protected marriage and virginity
13144.summary: He explains the laws on virginity, adultery, rape and fornication as perfect law that protected women and men and deterred immorality.

13156.title: Thou shalt not oppress him
13156.summary: As Israel was not to return an escaped servant, the church must not hold a repentant brother's past sins against him, since we too were bondmen in Egypt.

13157.title: Repent of sins teachers are least forgiving
13157.summary: He observes that churches teaching repentance of sin as a condition of salvation become self-righteous and unforgiving, having lost grace and humility.

13158.title: No whore nor sodomite in Israel
13158.summary: He refutes readings that make the sodomite a temple prostitute, teaching whores and sodomites were not to be tolerated nor their wages taken for vows.

13159.title: Lend not upon usury to thy brother
13159.summary: He teaches believers should back a brother in need or enterprise without interest, within a jubilee limit, while noting the stranger clause has been abused.

13180.title: Muzzle not the ox
13180.summary: He shows Paul used the ox treading corn to teach that those who preach the gospel should live of the gospel, and that the forty stripes rule shows judging by the letter, not rightly.

13211.title: The curses of Deuteronomy 28 on America
13211.summary: He teaches a nation whose people are faithful receives God's blessings, and that America squandered them and now suffers the curses of Deuteronomy 28.

13242.title: Choose life: Christ the end of the law
13242.summary: He teaches the law set life and death before Israel, its righteousness proving the need for the righteousness of faith, for Christ is the end of the law to all who believe.

13244.title: Choose life: against Calvinists and Zionists
13244.summary: Against dispensationalists, Calvinists and Zionists he teaches that God makes salvation an individual choice of the heart, Jews included, not forced or by birth.

13245.title: From glory to glory by the Spirit
13245.summary: Believers are at liberty and not judged by the law, yet beholding God's glory they are changed by the Spirit if they choose, not by rules men use to lord over others.

13249.title: What is written is sufficient
13249.summary: Against a Catholic claim from John 20-21 of unwritten oral doctrines, he shows those verses speak of signs and say the written word is sufficient to believe and have life.

13250.title: More blessed to give: not oral tradition
13250.summary: He answers the Catholic use of Acts 20:35 by showing Christ taught the same in Luke 6:38, so the written word, not tradition, preserves His teaching.

13251.title: The tradition Paul gave is written
13251.summary: He shows Paul's tradition in 2 Thessalonians 3 is written in the epistle and that 2 Peter 1 says scripture came by the Holy Ghost, the opposite of Catholic claims.

13270.title: The law was perfect, the fault the people's
13270.summary: With Joshua as a picture of Christ, he teaches the song of Moses shows the covenant failed because of the people, not the law, which disproves dispensationalism.

13308.title: Meditate therein day and night
13308.summary: As with Joshua, believers are saved by faith and blessed in this life by loving and keeping God's word, so be strong and not afraid.

13348.title: Obeying the spirit of the command
13348.summary: Joshua's order for silence shows careful obedience that guards against temptation, which is separation, not legalism.

13349.title: All things are not expedient
13349.summary: Though at liberty in Christ, believers keep standards like sobriety, modest dress and short hair for men to honor the spirit of God's commands and be a good witness.

13355.theme: The old man and the new
13355.title: Beware the sin of Achan
13355.summary: Like Achan, believers are often tempted to covet right after God gives victory, so we must stay on God's path even in success.

13413.title: It was of the Lord to harden their hearts
13413.summary: God hardened the hearts of the abominable Canaanites so they came against Israel to be destroyed, which he says is reprobation.

13423.title: One gospel: all are 1 Corinthians 15 Christians
13423.summary: He refutes the teaching that Paul preached a different gospel from Jesus and Peter, showing 1 Corinthians 15 is the same gospel of the same risen Christ for all.

13426.title: Bullingerism, a false gospel
13426.summary: He traces the Grace Movement to Bullinger and O'Hair and refutes its claim of different gospels in the Gospels, early Acts and Paul's epistles.

13428.title: The mystery: Gentiles fellow heirs
13428.summary: He teaches the mystery revealed to Paul is that Gentiles are fellow heirs of the same body by the same gospel, preached to Abraham from the beginning.

13462.title: Driving out the Jebusites
13462.summary: As Israel left Canaanites who became a canker, believers leave sins in their lives out of laziness, though God is faithful to deliver us.

13534.title: Our promises and blessings are related
13534.summary: The two and a half tribes kept their vow and received what they asked, showing God grants obedient children's petitions that agree with His will.

13535.title: Seek first His will: not a prosperity gospel
13535.summary: From his own life he teaches that seeking God's will first brings spiritual blessings and enough material provision, which is not a prosperity gospel.

13544.title: Phinehas heard them before judging
13544.summary: Distance breeds misunderstanding, and Phinehas shows right judgment by asking and listening before acting instead of accusing.

13545.title: Inquire meekly, then rebuke false ways
13545.summary: Believers should hate every false way but meekly ask professing Christians what they mean, testing them by the gospel before rebuking or accepting them.

13553.title: Be strong and of a good courage
13553.summary: Joshua's charge teaches that a peaceful, profitable life in Christ requires courage to obey God's commands, separate from the world and leave an example for our children.

13554.title: The true purpose of God's commandments
13554.summary: Beyond being a schoolmaster and for the lawless, the law's real purpose is to show the saved God's will for a successful life, not to earn salvation.

13591.title: Why God left the Canaanites in the land
13591.summary: God left the heathen in the land to test Israel, and tribulation and evil today likewise test us and humble men to call on Christ.

13593.title: Hard times turn us to the Lord
13593.summary: As Israel turned to God in hard times and fell away in good, God uses tribulation to prove us and work patience, experience and hope.

13595.title: It is always a choice
13595.summary: Israel chose of their own free will to leave the work undone, and God gave His word as testimony so men would believe, using even their disobedience for His purpose.

13596.title: The covenant was glorious, the fault was theirs
13596.summary: He argues Calvinism makes the covenants, the law as schoolmaster and Christ's obedience meaningless and limits God, whose will is done despite man's disobedience.

13605.title: The strength that comes from submission
13605.summary: Deborah and Jael show godly women used mightily within God's order of authority, while God wants strong men of faith to lead their homes.

13617.theme: Fear is a lack of faith
13617.title: Have not I sent thee?
13617.summary: Like Gideon, believers often ask for a sign to put off doing what they know God wants, when His word should be sign enough.

13618.theme: Fear is a lack of faith
13618.title: Tearing down his father's altar
13618.summary: Saved believers surrounded by false religion, even family, should stand for the Lord like Gideon, since faithful obedience convinces others more than words.

13630.theme: Fear is a lack of faith
13630.title: Lord, help thou mine unbelief
13630.summary: God helps our unbelief by testing our faith, as He cut Gideon's army to 300, making us weaker that we may become strong.

13632.title: The battle is already won
13632.summary: Trials are not for proving ourselves alone; growing faith means leaning more on God, who has already given us the victory.

13643.theme: The old man and the new
13643.title: Gideon's ephod became a snare
13643.summary: Gideon let success lead him to make an ephod and draw Israel away, a trap for successful Christians and preachers whose pride undoes their work.

13653.title: Great men and their wicked sons
13653.summary: Godly fathers often have wayward sons, so parents must picture God's grace without enabling sin, as with Jack Hyles, whose failures do not undo God's works.

13672.title: Jephthah's needless vow
13672.summary: God does not need our vows to deliver us, so we should not bargain with Him by vowing, but if we vow we must pay it.

13676.theme: Christ the foundation of the church
13676.title: A healthy church keeps its shibboleths
13676.summary: He welcomes the charge that fundamentalists keep shibboleths like separation and the KJB, the main one being the gospel of grace by which false teachers are known.

13696.title: We do not inherit sin
13696.summary: He teaches Ezekiel 18:20 refutes using Psalm 51:5 for original sin, so infants who die are not condemned and go to Heaven.

13697.title: Alive without the law once
13697.summary: He shows original sin relies on corrupt versions like the NIV and leads to infant baptism and limbo, while Romans 7:9 shows we die spiritually when we knowingly sin.

13698.title: God judges the heart, not ignorance
13698.summary: God does not impute sin to those without understanding, as with manslaughter and meat offered to idols, because sin comes from the heart.

13712.title: Christ our Passover, not a wafer
13712.summary: At Easter he teaches Christ, the Passover lamb, is the bread of life by one finished sacrifice, not a wafer or cup of wine.

13732.title: Samson's one line
13732.summary: Like Samson keeping only his hair while breaking the rest of his vow, Christians set an arbitrary line to feel right with God while sinning around it.

13742.title: Micah's house of gods
13742.summary: Micah, zealous but not after knowledge, built his own church of images with a priest called father, against God's word.

13807.title: Abominations as capital crimes
13807.summary: He teaches God's perfect law protects the innocent and that treating abominations as capital crimes is love, while teaching tolerance of sodomites is wicked.

13833.title: Get right with God before the battle
13833.summary: Even with a righteous cause, as Israel against Benjamin, we cannot expect God's help until we are right with Him ourselves.

13868.title: Spread thy skirt over thine handmaid
13868.summary: Ruth at Boaz's feet pictures the believer calling on Christ, our near kinsman, to cover and protect us.

13879.title: The law could not redeem, Boaz could
13879.summary: The nearer kinsman pictures the law, able to keep land but not redeem the person, while Boaz pictures Christ, who redeems us and raises the dead to their inheritance.

13889.title: God opens and closes the womb
13889.summary: He teaches God opens the womb and children are a blessing born innocent, condemning birth control, abortion and IVF as sacrificing children to Moloch.

13900.theme: The church is the Israel of God
13900.title: Eli's house cut off, a faithful priest raised
13900.summary: The cutting off of Eli's house pictures the end of the Levitical priesthood and the old testament, replaced by Christ the High Priest and the New Testament believers as His royal priesthood.

13905.title: The word of the Lord was precious
13905.summary: As in Samuel's day there is no open vision now, but we have God's full revelation in His word and need no private interpretation, so the word should be kept precious.

13913.title: God is not bound to Israel after the flesh
13913.summary: Israel was only ever spared for the sake of Christ the promised Seed, and like Israel bringing the ark to battle, dispensationalist Zionists wrongly trust in a covenant rather than in the Lord.

13919.title: Dagon fallen before the ark
13919.summary: The fall of Dagon before the ark shows God curses any attempt to mix His word and testament with idolatry, as Rome does.

13934.title: Golden emerods and apostate superstitions
13934.summary: Like the Philistines' made-up trespass offering, apostate churches acknowledge the true God but invent rites, sacraments and superstitions that are as profane to Him.

13935.title: To whom much is given, much is required
13935.summary: The men of Bethshemesh were punished more than the Philistines because they knew better, a warning that believers who know God's word are chastened more severely when they stray.

13948.title: God judges by giving men what they ask
13948.summary: One of God's sharpest judgments is giving men what they foolishly demand, and no one is saved, chastened or given over without full understanding of the truth and its consequences.

13981.title: Israel wanted a king they could see
13981.summary: Like Israel demanding a visible king, natural men in false churches want idols, rites and a man as head of the church rather than faith in the unseen promise of God.

13983.title: No political solution to a spiritual problem
13983.summary: Government matters less than the hearts of the people, so the answer to wicked rulers is not a king or politics but repentance, soul winning, godly homes and churches.

13989.theme: Christ our King and High Priest
13989.title: A man after God's own heart
13989.summary: Saul's unlawful sacrifice cost him the kingdom, while David, the man after God's heart, foreshadows Christ who is both King of kings and an acceptable High Priest forever.

13990.theme: The old man and the new
13990.title: A battle is not the war
13990.summary: After God gives a restored Christian small victories, spiritual enemies rally, so we must be more vigilant and wait on Christ rather than lean on our own understanding as Saul did.

14002.title: Saul's foolish vow added works to faith
14002.summary: Jonathan's victory was won by faith, and Saul's commanded fast, adding works of righteousness and doctrines of men, only weakened the people and led them into sin.

14005.title: Saul was saved, yet his end was tragic
14005.summary: Saul was truly saved by grace through faith, but a believer who forgets God's word and will not confess when chastened can lose his blessings and even be called home early.

14014.title: God gives many chances, but chastens compromise
14014.summary: Saul never lost his salvation but became a castaway, showing obedience is not for salvation but saved people are held to a higher standard and chastened for compromise and the sins they find appealing.

14016.title: To obey is better than sacrifice
14016.summary: False religion offers its own righteousness and costly works instead of believing on Christ's righteousness, which God calls rebellion and witchcraft.

14024.title: The Lord looketh on the heart
14024.summary: Man looks on the outward appearance but God on the heart, which reconciles Romans 4 and James 2: we are justified before God by faith and before men by works.

14030.title: The battle is the Lord's
14030.summary: David's victory over Goliath was the Lord's, teaching that our deliverance and victories come not by our own works or weapons but by God.

14032.theme: Christ our King and High Priest
14032.title: The giant-slayer's reward and our liberty
14032.summary: The king's promised reward for slaying Goliath pictures what Christ gives by faith: eternal life, sonship and freedom from the wages of sin.

14063.title: Jonathan and David's covenant in the Lord
14063.summary: The covenant of Jonathan and David sworn in the Lord's name pictures salvation, and Jonathan's love above his own father and kingdom shows how we should love Christ and our brethren.

14083.title: Love your enemies and let God avenge
14083.summary: By sparing Saul and leaving judgment to God, David shows the perfecting faith Jesus commands: love your enemies, trusting the Lord to deliver you.

14084.title: Doing right against peer pressure
14084.summary: When friends urge vengeance as if it were God's sign, we must do what is right in the Lord's eyes as David did, rather than please men as Saul did.

14094.theme: The old man and the new
14094.title: Be sober, be vigilant after a victory
14094.summary: Right after a victory of faith David nearly sinned against Nabal and then took more wives, showing temptation comes hardest when we grow complacent after God blesses us.

14102.title: These things happened for our ensamples
14102.summary: The repeated accounts in Samuel are real events recorded for our admonition, not folklore, so we can trust the Lord delivers as David trusted Him.

14129.title: The two Sauls of Benjamin
14129.summary: King Saul was saved but backslid by pleasing men until God gave him an ignoble death, while Saul of Tarsus of the same tribe kept under his flesh lest he be a castaway.

14153.title: How are the mighty fallen: forgiving in death
14153.summary: David's lament for Saul shows Christians should forgive those who wronged them, even in death, leaving judgment to a just God.

14169.title: Blessed are the peacemakers
14169.summary: The most peaceful solution should always be sought, especially between brothers, because peacemakers are called the children of God.

14187.title: Leave vengeance to the Lord
14187.summary: Taking vengeance for oneself is sin in God's eyes, but forgiving, seeking peace and trusting the Lord to judge is the path of faith that delivered David.

14193.theme: The old man and the new
14193.title: Driving the Jebusites from Zion
14193.summary: David driving the Jebusites out of Jerusalem pictures driving sin from the heart, which is never permanent while we live in the flesh, so we must crucify ourselves daily.

14216.title: Seven hundred or seven thousand horsemen
14216.summary: The seeming discrepancy between 2 Samuel 8 and 1 Chronicles 18 is explained by comparing the accounts, and modern versions that alter it show a lack of faith in the preservation of the word.

14225.theme: Christ our King and High Priest
14225.title: Mephibosheth at the king's table
14225.summary: Mephibosheth, crippled and spared to eat at the king's table, pictures the sinner given grace by Christ, and we are to show others the same mercy.

14229.title: Be of good courage and play the men
14229.summary: Christian men should not cower or force outcomes in fear but behave valiantly, obey God and trust Him to give the victory.

14235.theme: The old man and the new
14235.title: How sin compounds: David and Bathsheba
14235.summary: David's sin began with neglecting his duty, showing that skipping prayer and the word leaves us open to temptation and that unconfessed sin compounds.

14249.title: The Lord hath put away thy sin
14249.summary: When David confessed, God put away his sin so he would not die, yet chastened him in this life, a model for how believers get right with God.

14250.title: I shall go to him
14250.summary: David's comfort at his infant's death shows young children who die are with Christ, refuting the teaching that original sin condemns infants.

14253.title: Giving occasion to the enemies of the Lord
14253.summary: God chastened David chiefly for giving the enemies of the Lord occasion to blaspheme, so believers must live blameless before others.

14342.title: David the king as servant
14342.summary: David's last words confess the Psalms were inspired and show him as a servant king, a picture of Christ and an example of esteeming others better than ourselves.

14343.title: This is all my salvation
14343.summary: David's everlasting covenant shows salvation was by God's grace in Christ regardless of his or his house's unworthiness.

14352.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
14352.title: The plague stayed at Araunah's threshing floor
14352.summary: The plague stayed at Jerusalem pictures God shortening the great tribulation for the elect's sake before the rapture and wrath, and David paying for the altar pictures Christ paying for our sins.

14353.title: Destroyed for lack of knowledge
14353.summary: Confusing passages are understood by comparing scripture with scripture, and Satan tempts by making us doubt or by our ignorance of the word, so Christians must study it daily.

14362.title: Forgive as God has forgiven us
14362.summary: Having been reconciled while we were God's enemies, we should show our enemies the same grace and forgive others as we ask the Father to forgive us.

14382.title: Solomon said nay: no queen mediatrix
14382.summary: Rome twists Bathsheba's petition to make Mary a queen mediatrix, but Solomon refused her and there is one mediator between God and man, Christ Jesus.

14453.title: The covenant with David kept in Christ
14453.summary: God's covenant of an everlasting throne was made to David, not to the Jews or any modern state, and is kept in Christ, yet its blessings are conditional and the saved are chastened when they sin.

14480.title: God chose David and Jerusalem, not the Jews
14480.summary: God preserved Judah for David's sake and for Jerusalem where Christ would die, not because the Jewish people were chosen, and their broken covenant was replaced by a new one, so reject dispensationalism.

14506.title: Idolatry and sodomites bring judgment
14506.summary: Judah's idolatry and tolerance of sodomites provoked the Lord, and America is headed for the same judgment for false religion and sodomites in the land.

14523.title: How long halt ye between two opinions
14523.summary: Most people avoid deciding, but preaching the gospel forces them to choose eternal life in Christ or rejecting God and being given over to a reprobate mind.

14535.title: Seven thousand who have not bowed
14535.summary: After great triumphs believers may feel despair and alone as Elijah did, but God always has a remnant and still has use for us.

14556.title: Ahab humbled himself before the Lord
14556.summary: Ahab's humbling delayed but did not prevent God's judgment, and nations whose leaders will not humble themselves before God face His just wrath.

14582.title: His way or nothing
14582.summary: Jehoram removed Baal but kept Jeroboam's false worship in God's name, like Roman Catholicism mixing paganism with the Lord, and worship done man's way is evil in God's sight.

14588.title: The widow's oil that never ran out
14588.summary: The widow's oil pictures the Holy Spirit, which pays the debt of sin and fills others without running out, the best inheritance a man can leave his family.

14590.title: Death in the pot
14590.summary: The wild gourds that poisoned the pottage picture false teachers bringing damnable heresies into a church, which the preached word of God cleanses.

14599.theme: Sowing the seed of the word
14599.title: Naaman and the seed by the way side
14599.summary: Like Naaman, many who hear the gospel confess it in the moment but never receive it in their hearts, as the seed sown by the way side.

14601.title: Saved but living in the old flesh
14601.summary: A saved person can return to the old life since good works are not automatic, so we should disciple and encourage rather than doubt their salvation or condemn them.

14610.title: Blessed beyond measure, and still we complain
14610.summary: Like Israel, Christians who take God's blessings and liberty for granted and are not thankful invite His judgment, while today we still have unprecedented freedom to serve Him.

14612.title: Once you begin, you are without excuse
14612.summary: Starting to do right (Bible reading, church, separation, witnessing) obligates us to continue, and though people will mock, we must be doers of the word and accept it as the Spirit working in us.

14617.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
14617.title: The Shunammite woman a picture of the tribulation
14617.summary: The Shunammite woman hiding through the famine and having her land restored by the king pictures the woman of Revelation 12 hid through the tribulation and the saints rewarded at its end.

14619.title: The light promised to David is Christ
14619.summary: Judah was spared only for the promise to David, whose light is Christ, and the failed first covenant shows the Jews have no promises apart from Christ, against Dispensationalism.

14633.title: Don't let your zeal fade like Jehu's
14633.summary: Jehu's zeal burned bright but faded, so believers should keep their zeal for the Lord burning steadily all their lives.

14652.title: Elisha's bones and the cult of relics
14652.summary: One verse about Elisha's bones is twisted by Orthodox and Roman churches to justify relic worship, which scripture calls unclean, showing why doctrine must come only from clear scripture compared with scripture.

14658.title: Remove the high places in our hearts
14658.summary: Like Judah's kings who left the high places, saved believers are chastened when they never fully commit, so we should have David's heart and remove the high places in our hearts.

14667.title: Remove the high places for your children's sake
14667.summary: A father who walks in God's ways and keeps his house unspotted from the world increases the odds his children will follow the Lord, though it is no guarantee.

14668.title: Provoke not your children to wrath
14668.summary: Christian fathers should not rule as fearful tyrants but correct their children with the rod while showing them the Father's love and mercy.

14682.title: Howbeit they did not hearken: the if/then covenant
14682.summary: Dispensationalists ignore that God's covenant with Israel was conditional, and He destroyed Israel when they would not hearken, a lesson for modern Israel.

14683.title: The Lord rejected all the seed of Israel
14683.summary: God rejected all the seed of Israel, keeping the Jews only until the promise of Christ came, after which unbelieving Jews were destroyed and God regarded them no more.

14687.title: Hezekiah broke the brazen serpent Nehushtan
14687.summary: The brazen serpent was a picture of Christ lifted up, but Hezekiah rightly destroyed it when it was worshipped, refuting Catholics who use it to justify images.

14704.title: Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief
14704.summary: We have the Spirit and scripture rather than signs, yet may ask God to increase our faith, and walking in the light and confessing sin gives us confidence that He hears us.

14705.theme: The old man and the new
14705.title: Hezekiah's pride after his recovery
14705.summary: After God delivers us we are prone to grow proud and comfortable as Hezekiah did, so we should praise the Lord for His mighty acts and stay humble.

14715.title: The spirit of Josiah, not Hezekiah
14715.summary: Unlike Hezekiah, content that judgment would not come in his day (the attitude behind the pre-tribulation rapture's appeal), believers should, like Josiah, lament sin and preach against it even facing tribulation.

14716.title: Revival forces men to choose life or death
14716.summary: Preaching and soul winning force people to choose life or death; some are saved, many harden themselves, and our job is to work the harvest and force the issue.

14717.title: Not peace but division: pressing loved ones to decide
14717.summary: Christians hesitate to press loved ones to decide for Christ for fear of losing them, but loving family more than Christ makes us unworthy of Him.

14722.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
14722.title: Jehoiachin lifted up out of prison
14722.summary: The fall of Jerusalem echoes the great tribulation, and Jehoiachin lifted out of prison midway through the captivity to eat at the king's table pictures the saved caught up out of great tribulation and clothed in white.

14734.title: Why the wicked devour the more righteous
14734.summary: As with Babylon against Judah, God raises up wicked nations to judge a fallen Christian nation, but those wicked nations will face His judgment too.

14740.title: Woe to him that giveth his neighbour drink
14740.summary: Habakkuk's woe pictures Babylon making nations drunk with abominations like Mystery Babylon, and is sound doctrine against drunkenness and the shameful things it brings.

14741.title: Dumb idols and the Lord in His holy temple
14741.summary: Idolatry is vanity, and those who bow, pray and light candles to statues today are as foolish as the idol makers, for the living God is not found in man's handiwork.

14751.title: Yet I will rejoice in the Lord
14751.summary: Like Habakkuk facing desolation, believers in great tribulation or personal trouble can rest and rejoice in the God of their salvation, who remembers mercy in wrath.

14758.title: Peace, peace when there is no peace
14758.summary: True men of God preach hard warnings of judgment as Zephaniah did, while false prophets today, seeker sensitive, prosperity and LGBTQ affirming churches, preach pleasant peace.

14778.title: Repent of your sins is the Galatian heresy
14778.summary: Teaching that one must turn from sins or show fruit to be saved is the same as the Judaizers' circumcision, making salvation finished in the flesh and falling from grace.

14779.title: Let us walk in the Spirit
14779.summary: Paul encourages believers to walk in the Spirit and bear its fruit, which shows the fruit is not automatic or outwardly obvious, rebuking fruit inspectors' hypocrisy.

14781.title: Easy believism accusers have fallen from grace
14781.summary: Those who call grace easy believism and say struggling believers are not saved unless they turn from sin are self-righteous Pharisees adding works, while Christ died for us while we were sinners.

14786.title: Seek ye the Lord before the day of His anger
14786.summary: Men are judged after death but nations are judged collectively on earth, so Zephaniah calls all the meek of the earth to seek the Lord before His day of wrath.

14790.theme: The church is the Israel of God
14790.title: The remnant of Israel and the daughter of Zion
14790.summary: Zephaniah's promise to the remnant applies beyond the return from Babylon to Christ's followers and all believers in New Jerusalem, whom the false Jews of the synagogue of Satan will come to worship before.

14810.title: Nineveh the wellfavoured harlot
14810.summary: Nineveh, the harlot selling nations through whoredoms and witchcrafts, shows the same spirit of Mystery Babylon that passed through the empires and remains today.

14811.title: The great commission is a command
14811.summary: Rather than ignoring the warnings, chasing hidden knowledge or hiding away, believers are to assemble together all the more and preach the gospel to every creature before the judgment comes.

14832.theme: The church is the Israel of God
14832.title: All nations from Abraham, and his seed is Christ
14832.summary: The genealogies show the nations descend from Abraham, but the blessing is to his seed Christ, so all in Christ are heirs, and the Jews' advantage availed nothing when they rejected Him.

14841.theme: Every word of God is pure
14841.title: Evil in the KJV does not mean sin
14841.summary: The KJV saying God does evil means calamity, not sin, as Webster's and Jonah 3 show, and church fathers cannot contradict God's preserved word.

14933.title: God remembers our sin no more
14933.summary: As Chronicles passes over David's sins, God does not impute the believer's sin and remembers it no more, so we should be as gracious to our brethren.

14934.title: Delivered and translated into the kingdom
14934.summary: Colossians 1 shows God has already delivered, redeemed and reconciled believers the moment they believed, so we should be thankful and extend that grace to others.

14943.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
14943.title: Singing psalms and hymns continually
14943.summary: David's psalm shows God wants His people to sing songs of praise and thanksgiving continually, in heaven, in the tabernacle and in Christians' hearts today.

14946.title: The son of David shall rule forever
14946.summary: God's covenant with David that his son would build a house and reign forever is a clear picture of Christ, which is why the gospels' son of David is messianic.

14957.title: Two tales of our lives
14957.summary: Like Chronicles passing over David's sin, the believer's sinful flesh was crucified and his quickened new man cannot sin, so God will not impute sin and remembers it no more.

14971.title: Delivered unto Satan, yet the spirit saved
14971.summary: God uses Satan to chasten His people, and Paul's delivering the Corinthian fornicator to Satan for the destruction of the flesh that the spirit be saved teaches once saved always saved.

14972.title: The powers that be are ordained of God
14972.summary: God uses rulers good and bad to judge nations, so believers should not violently rebel but be subject, humble themselves, pray and get right with God.

14979.title: Repent ye: John the Baptist's call to believe
14979.summary: Repent means to change your mind and believe, not to stop sinning, so those John baptized confessing their sins had believed and were saved, baptism being the answer of a good conscience, not its cause.

15000.title: Faithful servants made rulers in the kingdom
15000.summary: As David divided roles in his kingdom, the saved will be given duties and rule in the millennial reign according to their faithfulness, so we should use our talents to win others to Christ.

15014.title: Why Christ died in this manner
15014.summary: Every sacrifice from Adam onward pictured the Lamb slain, and the cross and resurrection had to happen before witnesses so that all nations could hear the gospel and believe without seeing.

15016.title: Thou too: the backslider's retort
15016.summary: A backslider rebuked will seize on any fault in the one reminding him of his sin to justify himself, and without sincere acknowledgment his words should be treated as lies.

15024.title: All things come of Thee: giving willingly
15024.summary: Beyond the tithe, all we have is God's, so we should give to the church, the brethren and missions cheerfully and willingly with thanksgiving.

15068.title: Two or three witnesses do not make truth
15068.summary: The law's requirement of two or three witnesses is a threshold before judging, not proof, so right judgment must still weigh what was said and by whom, and those who say case closed have prejudged.

15082.title: Mount Moriah, where God provided a sacrifice
15082.summary: The temple was built on Moriah where Abraham offered Isaac, a picture of Christ, and its cherubim were never bowed to, refuting idolaters who cite them.

15083.title: Jachin and Boaz, pillars of the promise
15083.summary: The temple pillars Jachin (He will establish) and Boaz (in Him is strength) picture the promise and strength of the Christ to come.

15096.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
15096.title: God's presence came with the praise
15096.summary: At the temple's dedication God's glory came when praise was made, not at the sacrifices, so believers who want His presence should keep a song of praise in their hearts.

15111.title: His mercy endureth forever
15111.summary: Christ is the mercy of God that endures forever, and 2 Chronicles 7:14 shows God's mercy on a humbled, praying people is the only answer to sin in a nation.

15125.title: Rehoboam's heavy yoke and Christ's light yoke
15125.summary: Solomon's reign pictures the millennial kingdom and his heavy yoke the law, while Christ offers the lighter yoke of grace and brings wrath upon the unbelieving world.

15133.title: Rehoboam humbled: the prodigal chastened
15133.summary: Like Rehoboam, believers who backslide after early blessing are chastened by God, who warns them by His word, and the prodigal who returns finds mercy in the Father's house.

15136.theme: Christ our King and High Priest
15136.title: The covenant of salt: true King and true Priest
15136.summary: The covenants of salt with the Levites and with David contrast the true king and priesthood with Jeroboam's counterfeit, picturing Christ as King and High Priest against the beast and false prophet.

15146.title: Swear not at all: be doers of the word
15146.summary: Judah's zeal-filled oath carried a burden God held them to, so it is better not to swear but simply do the word, since God respects faith rather than promises.

15147.title: Promises in zeal we cannot keep
15147.summary: Judah's open-ended oath bred hypocrisy and Asa still left the high places, showing we should rely on God's mercy rather than make promises in the flesh we cannot keep.

15149.title: Asa sought the physicians, not the Lord
15149.summary: Doctors and allies may be God's tools, but we must go to God first and trust Him, since His withdrawal of protection from the consequences of our sin is His sorest chastening.

15158.title: Jehoshaphat yoked with wicked Ahab
15158.summary: Jehoshaphat's alliance with Ahab shows the danger of yoking with the wicked to please men, who will use our loyalty to save themselves, so we should not sit with the wicked.

15162.title: Shouldest thou help the ungodly?
15162.summary: God's wrath on Jehoshaphat for helping Ahab condemns Christian Zionism today, which calls unbelieving Jews who curse Christ our greatest allies.

15163.title: Deal courageously: judging righteously as to the Lord
15163.summary: Jehoshaphat's charge to his judges to judge without respect of persons in the fear of the Lord is the calling of every Christian to serve justly, seek others' profit and obey authority.

15167.title: Jehoshaphat's assembly of prayer and praise
15167.summary: Because Judah had been brought back to God by revival, they could fast, pray and sing in tribulation and see God deliver them, as a believer walking in the Spirit can boldly ask God for deliverance.

15175.title: Women rule over them: men abdicating authority
15175.summary: God's order is for men to rule in the family and the nation, to be ruled by women is a shame and a curse, and when women usurp authority it is first the fault of men abdicating it, as Adam did.

15194.title: Joash and the rebellious son
15194.summary: Like Joash turning on Jehoiada, children kept by a godly father's holiness may seize on his flaws to set impossible standards and justify rebelling, then sink further into sin once that authority is gone.

15195.title: You cannot carry your children's salvation
15195.summary: Fathers must train up their children with the rod and the Lord's mercy without provoking them, but cannot impose their own salvation, since each child must have his own relationship with God.

15201.title: The bitter end of an apostate
15201.summary: Amaziah, who knew God's things but turned to idols, shows the apostate whom Hebrews 6 says cannot be renewed to repentance and whose destruction is greater.

15208.theme: The old man and the new
15208.title: Uzziah's pride: stay humble
15208.summary: Uzziah's pride over God's blessings cost him everything, reminding us that God's rewards are given so that others may see and believe, so stay humble.

15215.title: Jotham entered not into the temple
15215.summary: Jotham did right but never entered the temple, and his example shows that forsaking the assembly limits what a Christian can accomplish as the day approaches.

15216.title: Church trauma is no excuse
15216.summary: Like Jotham perhaps put off by his father's leprosy, those claiming church trauma are mostly justifying sin, while every believer should seek an assembly and edify it.

15229.title: The Levites were more upright in heart
15229.summary: As the Levites outdid the reluctant priests in Hezekiah's revival, older Christians in lukewarm churches should welcome young believers' zeal and join in soul winning.

15232.title: Bidding all to the Passover feast
15232.summary: Hezekiah's call to all Israel to the Passover, a picture of Christ, is like the king's wedding parable where many made excuses but bad and good were compelled to come and were pardoned.

15233.title: Turn again unto the Lord, the remnant
15233.summary: Hezekiah preached to Israel's remnant that God's wrath could still be turned away, and 2 Chronicles 7:14 is a standing promise, so even in a wicked nation we compel men to return to the Lord.

15264.title: Josiah a model of the Christian life
15264.summary: Josiah's seeking God, purging idols, repairing the temple, being convicted by the found law and covenanting to serve God pictures the path a believer can choose to follow.

15272.theme: The church is the Israel of God
15272.title: Loammi: ye are not my people
15272.summary: Hosea's children declare God's mercy removed from Israel and that they are not His people, refuting dispensationalism, while the promise of sons of the living God is fulfilled in Christ.

15276.title: A door of hope: Ishi, not Baali
15276.summary: Hosea's door of hope in the valley of Achor is Christ the door, and calling God Ishi (husband) rather than Baali promises the close relationship we have in Christ.

15279.title: Hosea buys back the adulteress
15279.summary: Hosea's redeeming an adulteress pictures God expecting faithfulness from Israel through desolation, because in the latter days they would seek the Lord and David their king, who is Christ.

15288.theme: Now is the day of salvation
15288.title: Before it is too late, reprobate
15288.summary: The false idea that it is never too late to be saved has led many to Hell, since men who put off grace harden their hearts like Pharaoh, so seek peace in Christ while you can.

15293.title: I desired mercy, and not sacrifice
15293.summary: The sacrifices only pictured Christ, the one true offering, and God's will is that we know Him and show others the mercy He showed us, unlike goodness that fades like the morning dew.

15304.title: The great things of my law counted strange
15304.summary: Today Bible fundamentalism is mocked as strange by seminary-trained scholars, but like Israel's traditions of men this is folly, so we must study to be approved of God and compare scripture with scripture.

15307.theme: The church is the Israel of God
15307.title: Wild grapes, the wild olive and the true vine
15307.summary: God found the patriarchs as wild grapes, as the Gentiles are a wild olive grafted in, and Christ is the root and true vine from which unbelieving Ephraim is cut off.

15326.title: Out of Egypt have I called my son
15326.summary: As God called Israel out of Egypt, so He called His Son, and as Israel turned from Him so Christ's own received Him not, though God chastens to bring men to repentance rather than to destroy.

15329.title: God is not in the wind
15329.summary: Ephraim fed on the wind as the world chases winds of doctrine and clouds without water, but God is in the still small voice in our spirit, keeps a remnant, and has work for us.

15330.title: The Lord hath a controversy with Judah
15330.summary: Judah, representing the saved, still had sin God would scourge, but He calls His backslidden sons to turn to Him, keep mercy and wait on Him to be forgiven.

15336.theme: The old man and the new
15336.title: Blessing should humble us
15336.summary: Israel turned to sin in the abundance God gave when they humbled themselves, so believers should let blessing humble them and stay grateful in good times and bad.

15339.title: Take with you words: Hosea's sinner's prayer
15339.summary: Hosea's final appeal is a sinner's prayer: by confessing with our mouths we receive the free gift of eternal life, not by idols or our own works, and God heals our backsliding.

15345.title: Preaching Christ from Micah
15345.summary: Christ could be preached from Micah as Philip preached from Isaiah 53, since the Old Testament is entirely about Jesus and salvation has always been by faith.

15348.title: Why do bad things happen?
15348.summary: The objection about evil dodges one's own sin, while the Bible is a book of God's judgments promising that evildoers will be repaid and the oppressed avenged.

15349.title: The wicked hate the preaching of the law
15349.summary: The wicked try to silence preaching that shames them, yet they will be judged by the books at the Great White Throne, and believers' meekness exposes their petty wickedness.

15350.title: The breaker is come up: God visits evil on evil
15350.summary: Micah's gathered remnant is the Israel of God by faith, and we can take comfort that bad things happen because men choose evil, and God repays evil upon the wicked.

15354.title: Priests that teach for hire
15354.summary: Micah's false prophets who preach peace for money are today's feel-good preachers like Joel Osteen and the Catholic church, who put riches above truth and are under God's wrath.

15371.title: Micah 5: the ruler out of Bethlehem
15371.summary: Micah 5 plainly foretells Christ's birth in Bethlehem, His smiting and His everlasting goings forth, so unbelieving Jews who deny He is in the Old Testament are liars.

15376.title: Do justly and walk humbly with thy God
15376.summary: God is pleased not by blood offerings, which only pictured Christ, but by faith, mercy and judgment, and religious trappings without faith are dead works.

15384.title: I will wait for the God of my salvation
15384.summary: When leaders, friends and even family cannot be trusted, as Jesus said following Him brings division, we look to the Lord and wait for Him to deliver us.

15471.title: Don't make God send the storm
15471.summary: Christians who run from preaching like Jonah are still used by God, so stop running and dedicate yourself to soul winning.

15474.title: Crying unto the Lord from the depths
15474.summary: Jonah's prayer, like David's Psalms, shows the believer in distress turning to the Lord with thanksgiving, knowing He hears and delivers even from the depths.

15475.title: They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy
15475.summary: Denying our sin forsakes God's mercy, while confessing it, as Jonah did, is for our sake that we may know His forgiveness and cleansing.

15554.title: They went out from us, never of us
15554.summary: Quoting a sermon, he teaches that someone who leaves the faith for another religion was never saved, because the sheep do not follow a stranger's voice.

15606.title: The truth dwelleth in us for ever
15606.summary: A believer can never lose salvation or fall into apostasy, because the truth dwells in him forever; one who departs to another belief never had the truth.

15617.title: The remnant are not chosen but seek Him
15617.summary: The remnant in Amos 5 is not a Calvinist election of certain men but the promise that whoever seeks the Lord shall live.

15618.title: He that endureth to the end shall be saved
15618.summary: Enduring to the end is about being saved out of tribulation and persecution, not about keeping eternal life, which cannot be lost.

15619.title: Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord
15619.summary: Performative worship and sacrifices without faith and mercy do not please God, as with Catholic and Zionist religion today, and such will face His wrath.

15624.title: Spared for David's sake and Jerusalem's
15624.summary: Judah was spared only for God's promise to David and for Jerusalem, pointing to Christ, not for the sake of the Jews.

15630.title: Jesus is the plumbline
15630.summary: The plumbline set in Israel in Amos 7 is Jesus, the perfect cornerstone and measure of justice, while Bethel's false priesthood pictures Rome.

15638.title: Jeroboam's religion a picture of Rome
15638.summary: The long-lived false religion of Jeroboam with its idols, feasts and priesthood is a prophetic sign of the Roman Catholic Church and its offshoots, which God will destroy.

15639.title: When worship becomes a burden
15639.summary: When a people turn from the true faith even outward worship becomes a burden to them, as with the loss of Sunday blue laws, and God then hardens hearts already hardened.

15642.theme: The church is the Israel of God
15642.title: The tabernacle of David raised up
15642.summary: Unbelieving Israel was disowned like the heathen, while the fallen tabernacle of David is raised in Christ for the remnant of Gentiles called by His name.

15649.title: We are the righteous remnant
15649.summary: Believers are the salt that withholds God's judgment, and when the salt loses its savour the remnant will be taken like Lot before His wrath is poured out.

15657.title: Cease ye from man
15657.summary: Proud men who trust in men, riches and idols will hide in the rocks from the wrath of the Lamb, while the meek inherit the earth.

15661.title: Children and the base rule a judged nation
15661.summary: Child rulers, dishonoured elders and promoted sodomites are not causes of coming judgment but signs that a nation is already under God's judgment.

15662.title: Haughty daughters and Christian modesty
15662.summary: God judged Judah's proud and vain women as well as its men, which is why Christian women are called to modesty, meekness and good works.

15694.title: God is through with the Jews
15694.summary: The return of Judah's remnant was needed only for the promise of Christ, so there is no end-times promise for the Jews as a people apart from individual faith in Jesus.

15704.title: Babylon's fall foretold by Isaiah
15704.summary: Isaiah's precise prediction of Babylon's fall to the Medes shows the sure word of prophecy, so we should listen when the Bible speaks of the end times.

15739.title: Be as bold and meek as Isaiah
15739.summary: Isaiah went naked three years to preach God's point, so we clothed in Christ's righteousness should not be embarrassed to win souls.

15741.title: Babylon is fallen, is fallen
15741.summary: As Babylon's fall signalled the end of Judah's captivity, the fall of Babylon in Revelation signals that God's wrath is nearing its end and Armageddon is near.

15746.title: Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die
15746.summary: Unlike those who feast in the face of death, believers with the hope of the resurrection embrace separation and discipleship in Christ.

15768.title: Wines on the lees well refined
15768.summary: The wines on the lees well refined of Isaiah 25:6 were filtered, weak juice and do not justify drinking alcohol.

15788.title: Trusting in Egypt is death
15788.summary: Egypt pictures the world and our old life of bondage, and God's children must not turn back to it for help in tribulation.

15797.title: Vengeance is His, He will repay
15797.summary: God's promised peace for believers cannot be separated from His just wrath on the wicked, so we praise Him that vengeance is His.

15821.title: What confidence is this wherein thou trustest
15821.summary: The world respects ornate high places and Rome's trappings, but humble trust in the Lord in weakness is the believer's strength.

15835.title: Thou hast cast all my sins behind thy back
15835.summary: Hezekiah praises God for salvation as a gift of grace, and those who refuse it have no hope, so today is the day to believe on Christ.

15841.theme: The old man and the new
15841.title: Spiritual triumph wounded by pride
15841.summary: Like Hezekiah showing off his treasure, believers often fall hardest through pride right after God has blessed them.

15842.title: Leaving the consequences to our children
15842.summary: Some sins bring lasting consequences on our children, so put them above yourself and turn quickly to the Lord when you err.

15845.title: Prepare ye the way of the Lord
15845.summary: Isaiah 40 foretells John the Baptist and Christ the Shepherd, shows the folly of images of God, and promises strength to those who wait on the Lord.

15870.title: The flaw was with them
15870.summary: The old covenant ended not because the law was flawed but because the people continued not in it, and a new covenant in Christ replaced it.

15874.theme: The church is the Israel of God
15874.title: Elect according to grace, not heritage
15874.summary: Isaiah 44:5 foretells Christians called the Lord's, Jews claiming Jacob, and others claiming Israel, while God's elect are elect by grace.

15881.theme: The church is the Israel of God
15881.title: Surnamed by the name of Israel
15881.summary: Christians become the elect of Israel by adoption, called by His name and given a new name like Jacob.

15909.title: They always looked for the Christ
15909.summary: It is false that Old Testament believers did not know a Christ would come; Moses, the prophets, Simeon and Anna looked for Him by faith.

15910.title: Promises fulfilled grow our faith
15910.summary: Each prophecy God fulfilled, like Judah's return, is a reason our faith can grow that the Holy One would redeem all nations.

15933.title: Come, buy without money and without price
15933.summary: Isaiah 55 echoes Jesus' call to come and drink freely, salvation by grace at no cost, and the word as seed that will not return void.

15950.title: The fast that God has chosen
15950.summary: God rejects public fasting to be seen of men; the fast He chooses is to loose burdens and serve the needy in secret.

15951.title: Call the sabbath a delight
15951.summary: The Sabbath in Isaiah 58 is spoken of as Him, Christ, and keeping it means resting in Jesus and lifting the burdens of others.

15954.title: Cry aloud and spare not
15954.summary: Teaching that God is not angry at a Christian's sin is antinomian false doctrine, since God chastens every son He receives.

15956.title: Your iniquities have separated you
15956.summary: Trouble comes not from God's inability to save but because our sins separate us from Him so He will not hear, and Christ our intercessor gives us His armour.

15964.title: Hephzibah and Beulah, the bride
15964.summary: The bride married to the Lord is the New Jerusalem, and Judah was spared only for David's promise and the place of His name, never for the Jews themselves.

15965.title: The temple mount debate doesn't matter
15965.summary: Which hill the temple stood on does not matter, and any third temple will not be God's; Jerusalem is the Lord's and He will repay.

15975.title: Isaiah 61, the Christian's mission statement
15975.summary: The words Jesus read from Isaiah 61 are also every Christian's mission to preach the gospel, before the day of vengeance and the resurrection of the righteous.

15981.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
15981.title: For the elect's sake those days shortened
15981.summary: Believers plead for mercy not on their own righteousness, which is filthy rags, and God will shorten the days and spare His people His wrath.

15985.title: New wine found in the cluster
15985.summary: Isaiah 65:8 does not endorse alcohol: it is a descriptive parable, and new wine is fresh juice.

15986.title: No Mandela effect in God's word
15986.summary: Claims that the Bible was changed by a Mandela effect are blasphemy, because God's word is preserved and does not change.

16005.title: Daniel's meek appeal to authority
16005.summary: Daniel shows how to honour authority without compromising faith, against today's rebellion that is as the sin of witchcraft.

16017.title: Prophecy proves an omniscient God
16017.summary: The precise prophecies of Daniel prove an omniscient God, so we can trust His promises of eternal life and the resurrection.

16018.title: The stone cut out without hands
16018.summary: The empires of Nebuchadnezzar's image came to pass, and Christ is the stone that breaks them and the head of the corner, so we cannot doubt God's promises.

16024.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
16024.title: The mark of the beast and the saints
16024.summary: As with the golden image, the beast will make war on the saints, which refutes pre-trib, and those who endure will be gathered by Christ before the wrath.

16028.title: Chastening of the proud believer
16028.summary: Like Nebuchadnezzar, a prideful backslidden believer may be chastened by God, even with mental affliction.

16046.title: Daniel 7 and the Revelation
16046.summary: Daniel's vision of the beasts parallels Revelation's end-times events, and his fulfilled prophecies show this one is just as sure.

16054.title: The spirit of Daniel's prayer
16054.summary: Daniel's humble, contrite prayer seeking mercy for his people should matter more to us than debates over the prophetic timeline.

16055.title: The seventy weeks point to Jesus
16055.summary: Daniel's 69 weeks from the decree to rebuild Jerusalem land on Christ's ministry and His being cut off, showing the power of God's word.

16058.title: Daniel saw a glorified Jesus
16058.summary: The man in linen of Daniel 10 matches John's vision of Christ in Revelation 1, so he believes it was a pre-incarnate appearance of Jesus.

16059.title: Persist in supplication
16059.summary: The 21-day delay matching Daniel's three weeks of prayer teaches us to keep praying when we do not see an immediate answer.

16074.title: Antiochus a type of the man of sin
16074.summary: Antiochus IV pictures the coming Antichrist who will bring false peace, betray the Jews, declare himself God in Jerusalem with a living image, and begin the great tribulation.

16080.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
16080.title: Every one found written in the book
16080.summary: The deliverance in Daniel 12 is for everyone in the book of life, including Christians, refuting a pre-tribulation rapture.

16081.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
16081.title: Blessed is he that waiteth
16081.summary: Daniel's blessing on him who waits to the 1,335 days is the same promise as Jesus' he that endureth to the end shall be saved.

16084.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
16084.title: Timeline of days in Daniel 7 to 12
16084.summary: He lays out Daniel's seven years as tribulation of the saints, the abomination, 75 days of great tribulation, then the wrath of God.

16119.title: Soul winning is soul warning
16119.summary: Like Ezekiel the watchman, believers who fail to warn the lost have their blood on their heads, so go soul-winning.

16128.title: Get over yourself and go door-knocking
16128.summary: Ezekiel obeyed far harder commands without hesitation, so Christians should overcome fear and pride and give the gospel.

16145.title: Silver and gold cannot deliver them
16145.summary: Covetousness is idolatry and riches cannot deliver in the day of wrath; you cannot serve God and Mammon.

16150.title: Open idolatry worse than secret
16150.summary: God counts the open idolatry of a whole people worse than the secret cults of its great men, and judges the nation for it.

16154.title: The mark on the foreheads
16154.summary: God's mark on the righteous in Ezekiel 9 is what the beast's mark copies, but God has sealed us with the Spirit unto redemption.

16161.title: The promise is to the faithful
16161.summary: The regathering promise of Ezekiel 11 is to the faithful, not to every Jew, as dispensationalists claim.

16166.title: The days are at hand
16166.summary: Like the proverb Ezekiel rebuked, last-days scoffers say His coming is delayed, but His word will come to pass.

16169.title: Untempered mortar and peace, peace
16169.summary: False prophets who tell people they are safe in their sins, like Osteen and Joyce Meyer today, will be exposed and made ashamed.

16173.title: Though Noah, Daniel and Job were in it
16173.summary: The righteous stave off a nation's judgment for a time, but when it comes only the saved are spared, though God often spares their families for His purposes.

16177.title: The vine tree does no work
16177.summary: The vine's wood does no work, just as believers are supported by the root, Christ, without works, while fruitless branches are burned.

16186.title: God's writ of divorce to Jerusalem
16186.summary: Ezekiel 16 is God's divorce of unfaithful Judah, worse than Sodom, judged by her spiritual state rather than lineage, with hope only in Christ.

16187.theme: Every word of God is pure
16187.title: Tekton and carpenter, no contradiction
16187.summary: Tekton and carpenter both mean a skilled builder, so there is no contradiction, and Christ the builder framed the world.

16198.title: The fathers have eaten sour grapes
16198.summary: Ezekiel 18 teaches against original sin: each man is judged for his own sin, and each generation must get right regardless of its fathers.

16199.title: Turn yourselves and live
16199.summary: Ezekiel 18's call to turn concerns national judgment and chastening, not eternal salvation, which cannot be lost.

16218.title: I will not be enquired of by you
16218.summary: God will not be enquired of by those whose hearts are not right and who flee from hard preaching against their sin.

16221.title: Compromisers and the old paths
16221.summary: Those who call standards legalism repeat Israel's compromise, and God eventually gives such people up to their delusions.

16223.title: The law given for our good
16223.summary: God's statutes are given for our good, that it be well with us, and pastors who call the law grievous sound like Satan in the garden.

16241.title: Blessed are they that do his commandments
16241.summary: Revelation 22:14 is Jesus' present exhortation to the saved, not a demand for works in eternity, where the curse is lifted.

16255.title: Seek first, not divination
16255.summary: Consulting anything but God may bring a false answer that serves His purpose to our hurt, so start with His word and prayer, content with His will.

16267.title: The Jews were never the heroes
16267.summary: The prophets show the Jews were always a stiff-necked, rebellious people under God's curse, against the Zionist view that they remain His chosen.

16299.title: Egypt a broken reed
16299.summary: Like Judah leaning on Egypt, believers must not lean on the world's supports, which God may remove so we depend on Him alone.

16300.title: That we may know He is the Lord
16300.summary: The fulfilled prophecies against the nations, which set the stage for Alexander and Rome, show God calling His shots and using all things to His will.

16308.title: America the tall cedar
16308.summary: Like Assyria the tall cedar, America will fall, and when depends on whether believers keep their savour by preaching, soul-winning and separation.

16325.title: The parable of the watchman
16325.summary: Every saved Christian is a watchman responsible to warn others of judgment, and those not warned have their blood required at his hand.

16326.title: Be pure of the blood of all men
16326.summary: Everyone can spare a few hours a week to go soul-winning with a church, so warn souls rather than pass by the burning house.

16329.title: The way of the Lord is not equal
16329.summary: Ezekiel 33 concerns physical judgment, not losing salvation; a backslidden believer's past works buy no pass from chastening, while a sinner who gets right is blessed.

16335.title: Doers of the word, not hearers only
16335.summary: Like Ezekiel's hearers who enjoyed his preaching as a song, many churchgoers hear without doing, but the word should change us.

16342.title: Jesus is the promised Shepherd
