16342.summary: When Jesus says I am the Good Shepherd He declares He is the Lord of Ezekiel 34, whose flock is believers, not Jews after the flesh.

16370.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
16370.title: Hal Lindsey's failed end times predictions
16370.summary: He shows that Hal Lindsey's date-setting and geopolitical readings of Ezekiel and Revelation all failed, yet still tainted how people read prophecy.

16379.theme: The church is the Israel of God
16379.title: Restored not for their sakes but His name's
16379.summary: God restored Israel from captivity not because they deserved it but for His holy name's sake, and sometimes He blesses us the same way to sanctify His name.

16380.title: The new heart promise fulfilled in Christ, not 1948
16380.summary: The promise of a new heart and new covenant in Ezekiel 36 is fulfilled in Christ for the Israel of God, not in the UN-created state of unbelieving Jews.

16386.title: The dry bones are the resurrection, not 1948
16386.summary: The valley of dry bones prophesies the literal resurrection and Christ's kingdom over the Israel of God, and dispensationalists wickedly give these promises to unbelieving Jews by applying them to 1948.

16390.title: Gog and Magog are the armies of the world
16390.summary: Ezekiel 38 describes the same post-millennial attack as Revelation 20, when Satan deceives the nations against the camp of the saints, not one or two modern nations.

16391.title: Gog and Magog mapped onto every generation's enemies
16391.summary: For decades Christians identified Gog and Magog with whatever nation was their current enemy, ignoring the scriptural timing that puts it after the millennium.

16392.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
16392.title: Dispensational Zionism confused the timing of prophecy
16392.summary: Dispensationalism and Zionism conflated Armageddon with Gog and Magog and replaced the simple timing of scripture with charts and failed theories.

16400.title: The New Testament clarifies Ezekiel's prophecy
16400.summary: Older non-dispensational commentators let Revelation separate the pre- and post-millennial battles that Ezekiel saw darkly, and it is fine not to know every detail.

16401.title: Don't break fellowship over prophecy timing
16401.summary: After weighing the theories on Ezekiel 38-39 and Revelation 20, he teaches that holding hard positions on prophetic timing is foolish when the saved will all witness it.

16410.title: Ezekiel's temple as the 2nd Temple that fell short
16410.summary: One theory is that Ezekiel's temple was God's design for the returning exiles' 2nd Temple, which fell short, though it does not fit the site neatly.

16421.title: A third temple would not have God's blessing
16421.summary: Ezekiel's temple cannot be a future third temple built by unbelieving Jews, because God would never accept sacrifices after Christ's finished work or dwell in a house of abominations.

16422.title: Judge a man's faith by his profession
16422.summary: We should judge whether someone was saved only by what they professed to believe about Christ compared with the Bible, not by their works or our likes.

16425.title: Separated chambers: keep your heart set apart
16425.summary: The priests' separated chambers picture the believer's call to separate from the profane and cleanse himself daily to be more useful to the Lord.

16426.title: No return to sacrifices in the millennium
16426.summary: The dispensational claim that temple sacrifices return in a Jewish millennium is another gospel, since salvation was always by faith in Christ's blood.

16432.title: Ezekiel's temple points to Christ the true temple
16432.summary: Ezekiel's temple was the high pattern for a repentant nation to restore God's glory, and Israel's falling short points to Christ who is the true temple.

16433.theme: The new heavens and new earth
16433.title: No temple in the eternal state
16433.summary: Ezekiel's temple cannot be in eternity because Revelation 21 says the Lord God and the Lamb are the temple of New Jerusalem.

16444.title: Salvation by faith, national promises by works
16444.summary: Individual salvation was always by grace through faith, but God's national promises to Israel were conditional on their obedience, and they failed and were cast out.

16445.title: Promises withdrawn when the people fail
16445.summary: With the priesthood changed the law changed, and like Saul and others, Israel lost conditional end-times promises by their own unbelief without making God a liar.

16446.title: Ezekiel's temple: the offer that will never be
16446.summary: Ezekiel 40-48 describes a kingdom God graciously offered Israel if they repented, which will now never be because they rejected Christ.

16447.title: Read Old Testament prophecy through the New
16447.summary: Differences between OT and NT prophecy are what could have been versus what will be, so we should scrap Darby and Scofield and read the OT through the NT.

16449.theme: The old man and the new
16449.title: Missed opportunities and restoration
16449.summary: Sin and self-will make us miss blessings God offered, yet the saved can still be reconciled and used if we turn and walk in His paths.

16462.theme: The church is the Israel of God
16462.title: Circumcision of the heart is what matters
16462.summary: Scripture moves from circumcision of the flesh to pleas for circumcised hearts until in the New Testament only circumcision of the heart counts, open to believing Gentiles.

16479.title: Living waters flowing out from Jerusalem
16479.summary: The river from Ezekiel's temple pictures the Spirit and the gospel flowing out from Jerusalem, with believers as fruitful trees by the river as in Psalm 1 and John 7.

16480.theme: The church is the Israel of God
16480.title: The inheritance was never exclusive to the Jews
16480.summary: Even Ezekiel gives believing strangers the same inheritance as the tribes, showing God's promises were always for all who believe on Christ, never a genetic favor to Jews.

16492.title: Mine house is waste: neglecting the local church
16492.summary: Like the Jews who built their own houses while God's lay waste, Americans chase leisure and riches while local churches die, so join and build up a soul-winning church.

16498.title: The unclean defiles the holy
16498.summary: As Haggai shows that holiness does not pass by contact but uncleanness does, we must cleanse ourselves from sin before God will bless our work.

16508.theme: The church is the Israel of God
16508.title: Salvation is the wall
16508.summary: Jerusalem's wall of fire shows God's salvation as His people's defense, and the kingdom is now for believers of all nations while unbelievers are cast out.

16512.title: The Lord rebuke thee: Joshua made clean
16512.summary: Joshua the high priest made clean without the temple pictures cleansing by grace through faith and points to Christ the Branch and corner stone, while railing against Satan is not God's way.

16521.title: The woman in the ephah carried to Shinar
16521.summary: Zechariah's woman of wickedness carried to Shinar pictures the spirit of the whore, Mystery Babylon of Revelation 17, delivered to her place.

16525.theme: Christ our King and High Priest
16525.title: The Branch, a priest upon His throne
16525.summary: Joshua's crowning prophesies the Branch, Christ, who is both King and High Priest after the order of Melchizedek.

16531.title: Did ye at all fast unto me?
16531.summary: God rejected the exiles' self-made fasts because what pleases Him is true judgment, mercy and care for widows and the fatherless, not religious ritual.

16543.title: Nations seeking the Jew fulfilled in Christ
16543.summary: The promise that nations would seek God with the Jews failed through their blindness and is fulfilled in Christ, with salvation by Jesus rather than by the nation.

16563.title: Thy King cometh, lowly and riding upon an ass
16563.summary: Zechariah 9 foretells Christ's entry into Jerusalem and His kingdom, and the war against Greece becomes the gospel's conquest, not modern Greater Israel.

16629.title: Ease made them forget grace
16629.summary: Centuries of protection left the Jews complacent and unready for Christ, so we should be content and steadfast in faith in good times and bad, not taking God for granted.

16639.title: Smite the shepherd: the wounds in His hands
16639.summary: Zechariah 13 foretells Christ pierced and wounded in the house of His friends, the smitten shepherd whose fountain cleanses His people.

16640.title: Once you drink the water of life
16640.summary: One who has truly believed the gospel will never utterly turn from it, because the indwelling Spirit leaves no room for the spirit of error and the elect cannot be deceived.

16650.title: The day of the Lord in Zechariah 14
16650.summary: Just before Christ returns with His saints, the Antichrist's nations take Jerusalem, then the Lord splits the Mount of Olives, pours out wrath and reigns from Zion.

16672.title: Laying the foundation with joy and weeping
16672.summary: The shouts and weeping at the temple's foundation picture the joy over a new believer whose foundation is Christ, and the remembrance of God's mercy in older saints.

16679.title: Faith in the promise, not knowing the means
16679.summary: Abraham was counted righteous for believing God's promise without knowing the means, so OT and NT saints are saved by the same faith.

16683.title: The Samaritans worshipped what they knew not
16683.summary: The Samaritans who offered to help build the temple mixed the Lord with their own gods, worshipping what they knew not.

16684.title: Ecumenism refused and persecution follows
16684.summary: Zerubbabel rightly refused the Samaritans' ecumenical offer, and like them false religions, Rome included, use governments to stop true churches and soul winners.

16691.title: We are the servants of God
16691.summary: When accused for the Lord's work, believers should neither proudly fight nor cower but humbly stand firm and trust God to deliver or to repay.

16710.title: Ezra's refused escort: faith or tempting God
16710.summary: Ezra trusted God without an armed escort, but there is a fine line between faith and tempting God, and help offered may be God's own means.

16721.title: Strange wives and the unequally yoked
16721.summary: Ezra's crisis shows that marrying unbelievers leads men into their spouses' abominations, though God showed grace to believing outlandish women in Christ's line.

16722.title: Mixed marriages: unwise but not always sin
16722.summary: He holds that racially mixed marriage is less than ideal and unwise for a nation but not always sin, while spiritually mixed marriage compounds it.

16723.title: Pastors should preach against mixed marriages
16723.summary: Pastors should always forbid dating unbelievers and counsel against racially mixed marriages, yet show grace to believers already in them.

16727.title: Ezra's mass divorce was not God's will
16727.summary: God hates putting away and never commanded divorce, so Ezra's mass divorce was man's idea and the guilty should have lost office instead.

16728.title: Do the hard thing, not man's compromise
16728.summary: Ezra took the easy way of divorce, but facing the results of sin we should wait on God, accept consequences and do the hard thing he prescribes.

16731.title: Nehemiah's gathering was conditional on repentance
16731.summary: Nehemiah's prayer shows gathering depended on turning to God, so modern Israel, born of pride and unbelief, is not a fulfillment.

16743.title: Many hands make light work
16743.summary: As all Judah pitched in on the wall, every member should use his gifts to build up his local church, and joining one is God's command.

16750.title: The enemies' tactics against Nehemiah
16750.summary: Nehemiah's enemies used threats, lies, flattery and betrayal, as the world does against believers, and the answer is to keep doing the Lord's work without fear.

16786.title: Constant vigilance to keep the people separate
16786.summary: Nehemiah's cleansing of Jerusalem shows how quickly people return to sin and why pastors and fathers must keep constant, hard vigilance for separation.

16789.title: Jacob have I loved: the table made a snare
16789.summary: Malachi shows the Jews already despising God's table 400 years before Christ, so God turned His name to the Gentiles because the fault was theirs.

16791.title: A godly seed: the promise was always Christ
16791.summary: The godly seed God sought is Christ, the singular seed of Abraham, and Israel's marriage covenant ended when they slew their Husband.

16795.title: The messenger and the Lord coming to His temple
16795.summary: Malachi 3 foretells John the Baptist and Christ coming to His temple, who will come again as refiner and judge.

16811.title: Mordecai's pride and rebellion
16811.summary: Mordecai's refusal to bow to Haman was proud rebellion against authority God told the captives to submit to, like Saul's stubbornness.

16841.theme: A line of faith since Abel
16841.title: Job: faith in God before Abraham
16841.summary: Job shows that men feared and called on the Lord before and outside Abraham's seed, so salvation by grace through faith was always offered to all people.

16849.title: Shall we not receive evil? His grace is sufficient
16849.summary: Job's patience and Paul's thorn teach that our suffering serves to glorify God's grace and humble us, for His strength is made perfect in weakness.

16853.title: Retribution theology is man's, not God's
16853.summary: Job's friends argue that suffering proves sin, but God's verdict on them shows this karma theology is human, not His.

16859.title: Who ever perished, being innocent?
16859.summary: Eliphaz accused grieving Job of hidden sin, but Jesus taught that tragedy is not proof of greater sin, so we should comfort rather than lecture.

16861.title: True things used to make false points
16861.summary: Eliphaz's vision uses true doctrine about God's holiness and judgment to make a false point, showing great lies are built on misapplied truths.

16866.title: Quoting scripture without comfort
16866.summary: Eliphaz quoted true proverbs but misapplied them to blame Job, warning us not to judge by appearance and lecture the afflicted.

16870.title: Job's longing for death and Paul's strait
16870.summary: Job's longing for death was trust in God's final summons, like Paul's desire to depart, but believers should redeem the time and leave the timing to God.

16871.title: Seeing Christ in Job is no anachronism
16871.summary: The Old Testament is all about Christ, so Job's Holy One and Redeemer is Christ and OT saints were saved by the same faith in the same Savior.

16887.title: How should a man be just with God?
16887.summary: Job sees that no man is righteous before God and none can plead his own righteousness without a mediator, the man Christ Jesus to come.

16891.title: The word is nigh thee
16891.summary: Against Zophar's claim that God's ways are unknowable, Deuteronomy 30 and Romans 10 show God's word, Christ, is near and can be known.

16895.title: All creation testifies of God
16895.summary: Against Zophar, Job shows that God reveals Himself through creation so every man knows Him, and He rules life, wisdom and nations.

16901.title: Though he slay me, yet will I trust
16901.summary: Job rebukes his friends as worthless physicians, teaching that silent love is better than lectures, while he trusts God and asks only why.

16908.title: There is hope of a tree
16908.summary: Job confesses that though man dies, he waits for his change, the resurrection to incorruption, like a cut tree that buds again.

16914.title: The wicked drink iniquity like water
16914.summary: Eliphaz's ancient wisdom describes the unbeliever's fear of death and his end in outer darkness and fire, the congregation of hypocrites.

16917.title: My witness is in heaven
16917.summary: Job's lament prefigures Christ's sufferings, and his witness on high is Christ the advocate pleading for sinners.

16925.title: Comfort the broken hearted, don't berate them
16925.summary: Bildad's curses on grieving Job show what not to do, since a friend's suffering is a chance to let God's light shine by comforting him.

16928.title: I know that my redeemer liveth
16928.summary: Job confesses his living Redeemer, Christ, who will stand on the earth, and his hope to see God in his flesh in the resurrection.

16932.title: The portion of a wicked man
16932.summary: Zophar spoke true wisdom at the wrong time: the wicked rich never have peace, their treasure perishes, so lay up treasure in heaven.

16939.title: The Lord taketh pleasure in His people
16939.summary: Against Eliphaz's claim that God doesn't care for righteousness, the Lord delights in His people's righteousness, and Eliphaz's accusations came from envy.

16967.title: How can man born of woman be clean
16967.summary: Bildad's question how man born of woman can be justified is answered in Christ, made a little lower than the angels, born of woman yet pure, who tasted death for every man (Hebrews 2).

16972.title: All creation testifies of His power
16972.summary: Job teaches that the heavens, earth and seas show God's power and glory to all men, so that by the things that are made they are without excuse (Romans 1, Psalm 19).

16977.title: Eternal torment, not annihilationism
16977.summary: Against the false doctrine of annihilationism, the hope of the hypocrite perishes when God takes his soul and the unbeliever goes to eternal torment, the smoke of which rises forever.

16981.title: We have the mind of Christ
16981.summary: 1 Corinthians 2:14 was written to carnal believers at Corinth, so walking in the flesh cuts a saved man off from the wisdom of God, which is found in the fear of the Lord and departing from evil.

16989.title: Clothed in righteousness, a father to the poor
16989.summary: Job's respect came from delivering the poor, the fatherless and the widow and wearing righteousness and judgment, and this should be the goal of every Christian man.

16990.title: Gravity before office, not after
16990.summary: Deacons and respected men must already be grave and sober before they are named, so young Christian men should put away the world's arrested development and seek sobriety, humble service and kindness.

16991.title: Older men, mentor the young men
16991.summary: Middle-aged Christian men, even those who think past sin has disqualified them from office, should accept God's forgiveness and be an example to the young men in their church.

16993.title: Young men, honour the hoary head
16993.summary: Young people mocked Job in his calamity, but young Christian men should honour and learn from their elders, knowing the troubles of age will come on all.

16996.title: Pure religion: service to others
16996.summary: Caring for the widow, the fatherless and the poor was always God's will, not new in the New Testament, and a Christianity centered on serving others for God's glory is the goal (James 1:27, Luke 4).

16998.title: Do not be as Elihu
16998.summary: Elihu is a picture of the pride of youth with false humility, and young men and babes in Christ who rush to give their opinions to their elders should learn real humility from him.

17003.title: Suffering defies neat explanations
17003.summary: Though God can use suffering to correct, Job's affliction was not for his sin, so the wise response to another's grief is humble presence and charity, not overconfident correction.

17007.title: Don't act like you invented the doctrine
17007.summary: Elihu repeats obvious truths while boasting of his wisdom, and Christians should pass on even basic knowledge with humility, since it is of the Lord.

17011.title: Strawmen and the Titus 3:10 rule
17011.summary: Like Elihu putting words in Job's mouth, bad-faith debaters reframe what you said, so keep to what the Bible says and reject such a man after the first and second admonition.

17032.title: The cornerstone laid before the foundation
17032.summary: God's answer from the whirlwind points to Christ the chief cornerstone laid at creation, the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world, with the sons of God being believers rather than angels.

17039.title: The wild beasts under His providence
17039.summary: God's questions about the wild creatures show that what man cannot control or understand is ordered by God's providence, and man, wild and stubborn like them, is sustained by His mercy.

17040.title: Job asks why, God shows Who
17040.summary: God answers Job's why by enlarging his view of Who God is, showing creatures that flourish under His care through suffering and danger without being abandoned.

17056.title: Only God can subdue the dragon
17056.summary: Leviathan pictures Satan and sin, which man cannot subdue, bargain with or tame, so Job, like us, is restored only by God's grace and the blood of Christ, not by his own righteousness.

17061.title: Job restored when he prayed for his friends
17061.summary: Job made peace with God by faith, but it was his forgiving and praying for the friends who wronged him, a picture of Christ the mediator, that led God to restore him double.

17062.title: Our later end greater than our former
17062.summary: Our trials are an opportunity to know God better and grow in faith, because in Christ our bondage is turned to liberty and our later end will be greater than the beginning.

17138.title: Like Job, our end better than our beginning
17138.summary: Like Job, believers pass through trials from the Accuser, but by grace through faith our end at the adoption and resurrection will be glorious, joint heirs with Christ.

17142.title: The fear of the Lord the beginning of knowledge
17142.summary: Proverbs was given to make men wise through the fear of the Lord, and parents are commanded to teach these truths to their children, the greatest inheritance they can leave.

17146.title: Wisdom crieth, and God will laugh at their calamity
17146.summary: Wisdom calls men to repentance as God did through the prophets and Christ, but those who hate knowledge are given over, and God will not answer but laugh when their calamity comes.

17148.theme: Every word of God is pure
17148.title: Every word out of His mouth
17148.summary: Since wisdom proceeds from the mouth of God and man lives by every word of God, we need a Bible that keeps every word, which in English is only the King James Bible.

17150.title: The paths of judgment and the way
17150.summary: The paths of Proverbs are the way, the doctrines of Christ, and discretion keeps us on them and delivers us from the evil man and the strange woman whose paths lead to death.

17153.title: Trust in the Lord, lean not on thine own understanding
17153.summary: Proverbs 3:5-6 is the key verse of the book: acknowledge God first and keep His old paths, and honour Him with your substance out of gratitude, not as a prosperity gospel.

17154.title: Whom the Lord loveth he correcteth
17154.summary: God's chastening when we stray is a mark that we are sons and should be received with thanks, and Wisdom, by which God founded the earth, is Jesus Himself, the way and the tree of life.

17156.title: Love thy neighbour; strive not without cause
17156.summary: Proverbs 3:27-32 is love thy neighbour, explained by the good Samaritan, and the froward, unyielding man who strives without cause is an abomination to the Lord.

17158.title: Get wisdom: a father's urgent instruction
17158.summary: As David urgently taught Solomon to get wisdom, every parent's priority should be to impart the fear and knowledge of God and keep children from those who cause them to stumble.

17166.title: The strange woman and the wife of thy youth
17166.summary: The strange woman of Proverbs 5 is both folly and literal adultery, which Solomon himself fell into, and the cure is to rejoice in the wife of thy youth and keep to God's straight path.

17169.title: Phylacteries and binding the word on the heart
17169.summary: Binding God's word on the heart means living it and letting it guide us day and night, not the Pharisees' literal phylacteries worn to be seen of men.

17170.title: Lust not after her beauty in thine heart
17170.summary: Jesus' teaching that lust is adultery in the heart clarifies Solomon's warning, and men today are ruined by pornography and online lust when they should delight in the wife of their youth.

17172.title: The harlot's snare and the goodman gone
17172.summary: The harlot's seduction of the simple young man is both literal and a picture of sin, whose lie is that the goodman, Christ, is far off and judgment delayed.

17174.title: Wisdom from everlasting is the Word
17174.summary: Wisdom in Proverbs 8, crying out to all and with God from everlasting before creation, is the Word, Jesus Christ, the way, the truth and the life.

17181.title: Reprove not a scorner; shake off the dust
17181.summary: As Christ and Paul taught, we do not argue with scorners when giving the gospel but shake off the dust and move on, while instruction to the wise makes them wiser, each man bearing his own guilt.

17182.title: Stolen waters are sweet
17182.summary: Folly, the strange woman, lures both the simple and the wise through covetousness, and sin lieth at the door, but her guests are in the depths of hell.

17185.title: The desires of the righteous granted
17185.summary: God repeatedly promises to grant the desires of those who trust and walk in His way, so we should ask for heavenly treasure such as serving God and winning souls.

17188.title: Riches profit not in the day of wrath
17188.summary: Riches cannot deliver from wrath but the imputed righteousness of Christ does, so the righteous give generously and lay up treasure in heaven rather than hoarding.

17189.title: The only surety we can count on
17189.summary: Being surety for others brings regret, but the only sure surety is God's, the Holy Spirit as the earnest sealing the believer's inheritance by Christ's finished work.

17190.title: He that winneth souls is wise
17190.summary: Sowing righteousness and bearing the fruit of the tree of life is winning souls, the greatest wisdom we can share and treasure laid up in heaven.

17195.title: He that spareth his rod hateth his son
17195.summary: A wise son comes from a father who loves him enough to chasten him, and God likewise chastens His sons, so a lack of chastening should make us ask if we are sons or bastards.

17196.title: Low time preference is a sign of wisdom
17196.summary: The wise son receives instruction and reproof, and his diligence and willingness to delay gratification for a later harvest is wisdom, while the fool's haste and greed destroy him.

17201.title: The scorner seeketh wisdom and findeth it not
17201.summary: Those who hate God are given over and never find wisdom, so the wise keep silent under accusation as Christ did and flee foolish teachers rather than sifting knowledge from them.

17202.title: A way which seemeth right unto a man
17202.summary: Because the heart is deceitful, the way that seems right to man ends in death, and the backslider is filled with his own ways, so we must keep our heart sound.

17203.title: He that hath mercy on the poor
17203.summary: Remembering the poor is done unto Christ and lent to the Lord, and since righteousness exalteth a nation we should win souls so it becomes a nation of Christians, not Christian nationalism.

17206.title: A soft answer and every idle word
17206.summary: A soft answer and pure words please God, but every idle word will be judged at the Great White Throne, which should drive men to the salvation that spares believers that humiliation.

17207.title: Out of the abundance of the heart
17207.summary: Our words are a window to our heart, and God, who sees hell and destruction, knows every thought and word.

17208.title: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination
17208.summary: God hears the prayer of the upright but the wicked's show of piety and self-made sacrifices are an abomination, since they go about to establish their own righteousness instead of submitting to God's.

17214.title: The lot is cast, the disposing is of the Lord
17214.summary: God gives the heart its words by the Spirit and disposes even the casting of lots, as in Israel's use of lots and the Urim and Thummim, showing His sovereignty and our acceptance of His will.

17217.title: The king's judgment and the powers that be
17217.summary: Rulers are ordained of God to punish evil (Romans 13), not by divine right to do as they will, and a wicked king is an abomination like an unjust weight whom God will repay.

17219.title: There is a way that seemeth right
17219.summary: Man can rationalize any sin, but God's ways are higher than ours, so we must acknowledge Him and study His word to walk His paths, which alone lead to life.

17223.title: Parents and children a parable of our walk
17223.summary: The relationship of parents and children, raising them in the nurture and admonition of the Lord, is a living parable of our relationship with God the Father and shapes their walk.

17224.title: A friend born for adversity
17224.summary: God tries the heart like a refiner, and a man of excellent spirit loves others as Christ loved us, being a friend and brother in adversity, forgiving and holding his tongue.

17231.title: Fools who follow their heart
17231.summary: The fool's delight is to follow his heart and find himself, but the heart is deceitful above all things, so do not be yoked with fools who corrupt wisdom to justify their lusts.

17232.title: The name of the Lord is a strong tower
17232.summary: The righteous run into the name of the Lord and are safe, while the rich trust in their wealth as a high wall in their own conceit, which will be their downfall.

17234.title: He that answereth a matter before he heareth it
17234.summary: Saints who will judge angels must judge righteous judgment among brethren, hearing the whole matter and the other side rather than the first story told.

17240.title: No respect of persons; lending to the Lord
17240.summary: Man naturally favours the rich and forsakes the poor, but James forbids respect of persons, and having pity on the poor is lending to the Lord, who will repay.

17241.title: It is a glory to pass over a transgression
17241.summary: As Christ taught to turn the other cheek, it is a glory to defer anger and let slights go rather than react like a fool.

17244.title: Wine is a mocker
17244.summary: Proverbs 20:1 plainly teaches that drinking wine and strong drink is not wise, and those who use the Bible to excuse drinking deceive themselves.

17245.title: The hoary head is a crown of glory
17245.summary: Honouring the old man is both wise and a command of God, since long life usually brings the fear of the Lord, knowledge and good counsel.

17247.title: All scripture, even Proverbs, is about Christ
17247.summary: Proverbs carries the gospel that none is righteous, and all scripture including Proverbs is about Christ the Word, through which faith comes by hearing.

17265.title: Train up a child in the way he should go
17265.summary: Training children in the fear of the Lord with the rod of correction, not by osmosis from a weekly service, guards them for life, as prudence means settling one's account with God now.

17269.title: The borrower is servant to the lender
17269.summary: Americans ignore God's wisdom on debt, diligence and giving while blaming the rich and the state, and the nation has removed the landmarks of the old paths and wonders why it is wicked.

17273.title: Be not desirous of his dainties
17273.summary: Believers are heirs and future rulers with Christ, so they must keep in check the appetites, riches and lust of the eyes that Satan and the powerful use to pervert their judgment.

17274.title: Cast not your pearls before swine
17274.summary: Fools despise wisdom, so whether online or soul winning door to door we should give our piece, reject the heretic after admonition, shake off the dust and not be trapped in debate.

17275.title: Remove not the old landmark of the fatherless
17275.summary: Stealing from the fatherless who have no one to plead for them brings God's vengeance, as with Ahab and Naboth, for their Redeemer is mighty.

17276.title: The rod, honest instruction, and wine
17276.summary: Children need both the rod and godly instruction, honesty from parents about their own sin, and warning against drink, which God says not even to look upon.

17282.title: Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the old men
17282.summary: Rehoboam sought a multitude of counsel but followed the young men over the old men who served Solomon, and lost the kingdom for lack of the wisdom his father wrote.

17283.title: When they say they are a good person
17283.summary: When soul winning, those who deny they sin can be shown Revelation 21:8 on all liars and Proverbs 24:9 that even the thought of foolishness is sin, while scorners are left behind.

17292.title: A just man falleth seven times and riseth
17292.summary: The righteous rise again even from death while the wicked fall, so we must not rejoice in their fall or fret and fear over them as many online Christians do, but trust God to repay.

17293.title: Meddle not with them that are given to change
17293.summary: Change for its own sake has led churches into apostasy, from Catholicism to modernism and the compromise of standards and music, and moving the landmarks of the fathers ends in sudden ruin.

17299.title: It is not good to have respect of persons
17299.summary: In judgment we must not favour the rich but weigh a man by his words, character and the full matter, and woe to those who call the wicked righteous.

17302.title: Princes under tutors until the adoption
17302.summary: Proverbs for kings and princes are for saved believers, co-heirs who will rule with Christ, since the adoption, the placing as sons, comes at the resurrection, the redemption of the body.

17303.title: Take away the dross from the silver
17303.summary: Walking in the Spirit and seeking God's wisdom refines believers like silver, giving the heirs the character to rule and judge righteously as vessels of honour.

17323.title: Answer a fool according to his folly
17323.summary: Proverbs 26:4-5 means we should not argue with a fool but rebuke him with scripture and then reject him, because a man wise in his own conceit is beyond hope.

17324.title: No doctrine on a parable alone
17324.summary: Fools misuse parables, and no doctrine should stand on a parable alone, as with Abraham's bosom, since Lazarus was carried to Abraham in heaven, not to a paradise compartment in hell.

17325.title: As a dog returneth to his vomit
17325.summary: Apostates who taste the truth and fall back, as Peter applies the proverb, are hardened into reprobation and return to their folly like a dog to his vomit.

17326.title: Wise in his own conceit
17326.summary: The man wise in his own conceit has made his esoteric opinions his identity and cannot be moved by scripture, which is why we reject him and shake the dust.

17329.title: Taking a dog by the ears
17329.summary: Meddling in others' fights, from church disputes to online drama, is folly, and likewise a godly nation should not join the enemies of Christ in their wars, as Jehoshaphat was rebuked for helping Ahab.

17330.title: Talebearers, evil surmising and discord
17330.summary: Lying for sport, talebearing and evil surmising kindle strife and sow discord among brethren, one of the things God hates, and such haters will fall into their own pit.

17340.title: Boast not thyself of tomorrow
17340.summary: Tomorrow is not promised, which makes today the day of salvation, so we should not boast or procrastinate nor be paralyzed by worry, but be prudent and diligent now.

17345.title: Iron sharpeneth iron
17345.summary: Christian friends sharpen one another and act as a mirror of our heart, as does scripture, and we should not forget what we see but be doers of the word.

17346.title: Know the state of thy flocks
17346.summary: Riches do not last, so diligently manage what God provides and, how much more, tend the flocks He has given us to serve, from a child to a church.

17368.title: The righteous are bold as a lion
17368.summary: The wicked flee in guilt, but believers have boldness and a clean conscience by the blood of Christ to come to the throne of grace, while wilful rejecters face fearful judgment.

17371.title: No political solution for a spiritual problem
17371.summary: A sinful land gets many oppressive rulers, and God gave Christians, the salt of the earth, the job of preserving the nation through revival in the church and soul winning, not the ballot box.

17372.title: They that forsake the law praise the wicked
17372.summary: Law-haters who use grace to excuse sin go on to praise the wicked, sodomites and rioters, while believers keep the law, abhor evil and honour the powers that be.

17377.title: The forgiveness of our debt
17377.summary: The law covenant put Israel in bondage to death, but Christ's blood is a better testament that forgives our debt, the grace God commands us to show others.

17382.title: He that turneth away his ear from the law
17382.summary: Those who use liberty in grace to excuse sin and teach that God is not mad at sin have abominable prayers, while believers should affirm the law and abstain so as not to make the weak stumble.

17386.title: The rich man is wise in his own conceit
17386.summary: The rich trust in themselves and resist the gospel, as soul winners find, while the poor seek the truth, though welfare can make them wise in their own conceit too.

17387.title: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper
17387.summary: With freedom to preach openly, Christians still hide, and believers must confess and forsake their sins, including neglect of church, Bible and soul winning, rather than harden their hearts.

17391.title: He that hasteth to be rich
17391.summary: Lack of understanding breeds covetousness, which prosperity-gospel con men and false teachers exploit, while the faithful man who works diligently abounds in blessings.

17412.title: Give me neither poverty nor riches
17412.summary: Agur's prayer for neither poverty nor riches shows we should be content with what God gives, since riches make men forget God and want makes them steal, as Paul learned contentment.

17413.title: Asking for more with a full pantry
17413.summary: With more plenty than we can store we still ask God for more, so we should practise gratitude and contentment as in Agur's prayer.

17418.title: Who art thou that judgest another man's servant
17418.summary: Accusing a fellow believer of his failings accuses his Master, so we should edify one another in meekness and remove the beam from our own eye first.

17419.title: There is a generation always with us
17419.summary: The wicked generation of Proverbs 30 is not one age group but the reprobates always among us, who despise parents and are pure in their own eyes (Romans 1).

17430.title: Give not thy strength unto women
17430.summary: Lemuel's mother warned against giving strength to women, the very thing that brought strife and blood on David's house and turned Solomon's heart.

17431.title: It is not for kings to drink wine
17431.summary: Believers are princes and co-heirs with Christ, so wine and strong drink are not for them, alcohol being allowed only as medicine for the perishing.

17432.title: Jesus dumb before His accusers, appointed to destruction
17432.summary: Christ, silent before Pilate and Herod, fulfilled Isaiah 53 and Lemuel's charge to open the mouth for the dumb, leaving the rulers of Judea without excuse.

17433.title: Biblical Christianity, not social justice
17433.summary: God's justice and care for the poor and fatherless are Christian virtues done personally and through the church, not handed to government or hijacked as cover for the guilty.

17491.title: Rich toward God, not laying up treasure
17491.summary: Hoarded riches are vanity because a man takes nothing with him, as the rich fool shows, so the good portion is to enjoy God's gift and be rich toward God.

17493.title: The curse of Adam behind the vanity of labour
17493.summary: The endless labour, unfilled appetite and death that make life vain are the direct result of Adam's sin and the curse on the ground.

17497.title: Say not the former days were better
17497.summary: Longing for better former days is a snare; there is no political solution to a spiritual problem, so we redeem the present time and give our children the wisdom of God.

17503.title: Not a just man upon earth that sinneth not
17503.summary: There is not a just man that sinneth not, the foundation of the gospel, so the fear of God humbles us to see our own sin and seek His grace.

17509.title: The snare of the strange woman and Eve's deception
17509.summary: Solomon's finding of few upright men and no upright woman, with 1 Timothy 2, acknowledges woman's nature to be deceived while she can still be the virtuous woman, equal in Christ and subject to her husband.

17520.title: Sentence against an evil work not executed speedily
17520.summary: Delayed judgment against evil emboldens the wicked and keeps them from fearing God, so opposing swift justice and the death penalty does the wicked no favors.

17527.title: Gold, silver and precious stones tried by fire
17527.summary: After death comes judgment: the lost at the white throne, the saved judged by Christ for reward, so live with eternity in mind and build works that abide.

17528.title: Your labour is not in vain in the Lord
17528.summary: Works done for the Lord are never in vain, and the good things of this life, a wife, food and drink, are gifts of God's grace to be enjoyed.

17533.title: Yielding to rulers, the example of Mordecai
17533.summary: A little folly ruins a wise man's name, and it is better to yield to a ruler than flee or fight, as Christ, the apostles and David did, while Mordecai's refusal to bow brought slaughter.

17539.theme: Sowing the seed of the word
17539.title: Cast thy bread upon the waters
17539.summary: Since we know not what tomorrow brings, give liberally and sow the word at every opportunity, boldly preaching Christ, and it shall not return void.

17544.title: Fear God and keep his commandments, the whole duty of man
17544.summary: After all is vanity, the conclusion is to fear God and keep His commandments, for every work will come into judgment and abundant life is in serving Him.

17562.title: I am black, but comely: Christ and His beloved
17562.summary: The Song pictures Christ and the saved: blackened by sin and servitude, yet made upright by His imputed righteousness and called fairest among women.

17565.title: Rise up, my love, and come away
17565.summary: The bride waiting for her beloved pictures believers waiting for Christ's return to gather His elect, while the wicked hide in the rocks from the wrath of the Lamb.

17570.title: The King's wedding procession and many crowns
17570.summary: The bride's search pictures the empty tomb and finding Christ, and Solomon's procession pictures Christ returning with His saints for the marriage supper and His kingdom.

17578.title: Brought back by tribulation, still sick of love
17578.summary: The backslidden believer may be brought back through persecution and tribulation, yet like the bride she will not renounce her beloved.

17579.title: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
17579.summary: The suffering bride's praise of her beloved describes Christ, divine and human, and her testimony under persecution moves others to ask why He is above all.

17581.title: Our testimony in persecution leads others to seek Him
17581.summary: The daughters who asked what made her beloved special now seek him with her, showing that a believer's faithful testimony through trials leads others to Christ.

17588.title: Set me as a seal upon thine heart
17588.summary: The seal on the heart pictures the unbreakable seal of the Spirit, and love that cannot be bought shows God's grace is unmerited, not purchased by works.

17589.title: The vineyard let out to keepers
17589.summary: Where Israel's husbandmen betrayed the Lord's vineyard, the bride freely gives Him its fruit and pays the keepers, as believers support pastors and missionaries with tithes and offerings.

17590.title: Make haste, my beloved: praying for His return
17590.summary: The Song ends in prayer for the beloved to come quickly, the believer's prayer of Maranatha for the day of the Lord, the gathering of His people and His wrath on the ungodly.

17639.title: Blessed is the man who meditates in His law
17639.summary: The blessed man meditates on God's word day and night and bears fruit, while those who attack or downplay scripture, as Satan did with Eve, are chaff.

17658.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
17658.title: Praise, gratitude and humility in prayer
17658.summary: The Psalms are a foundation for prayer, teaching us to come with praise, gratitude and humility, knowing any righteousness we have is God's.

17663.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
17663.title: Unto thee will I pray, morning and night
17663.summary: David's morning prayer models calling on God day and night, hallowing His name, asking His will be done and His enemies, the whited sepulchres, brought down.

17666.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
17666.title: Praise, humility, mercy, then judgment
17666.summary: Prayer should begin with humbling ourselves and seeking forgiveness rather than complaining, then turn to asking relief and judgment.

17667.title: Persistent prayer like the importunate widow
17667.summary: Scripture and Christ's parable of the widow teach persistent prayer for a matter while accepting His will, and gratitude for His answer often brings greater blessing.

17668.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
17668.title: Reminding God of His promises
17668.summary: Appealing to God's own promises in prayer shows we know and trust His word, and pleases Him.

17672.title: Search me first, then judge the wicked
17672.summary: In trouble we should ask God to search us and accept our part, then pray for His judgment on the wicked, for God is angry with the wicked every day.

17694.title: Love your enemies, yet pray for God's vengeance
17694.summary: We love our personal enemies, but may pray imprecatory prayers against the wicked who oppress the righteous, rejoicing that God's wrath will repay.

17695.title: Afflicted for doing the work of God
17695.summary: Believers who serve God, like a sister just after winning a soul, will be attacked, and should patiently endure so their faith grows and their light shines.

17699.title: The wicked lie in wait to catch the poor
17699.summary: The wicked, like their father the devil, set nets for the poor and fatherless through vice and scams, and though God's judgment seems delayed He will repay.

17703.title: Seeking to be wise, the scholars miss the forest
17703.summary: Studies obsessed with historical context, Hebrew and jargon miss Christ, the gospel and the prophetic application plain in the Psalms, and should be avoided.

17705.title: Have you ever cried out to the Lord for help
17705.summary: Nearly everyone has cried out to God for help, which opens the way to show them they must call upon the Lord to be saved.

17709.title: Modern versions corrupt the promise of preservation
17709.summary: The ESV changes Psalm 12:7 from God preserving His words to preserving men, casting doubt on preservation just as Satan asked, Yea, hath God said?

17712.title: My grace is sufficient for thee
17712.summary: An unanswered prayer may be answered by God's sufficient grace; remembering how He already delivered us keeps us from complaining like Israel in the wilderness.

17714.title: There is none righteous, no, not one
17714.summary: Psalm 14, quoted in Romans 3, is the definitive statement that all have sinned and need the gospel, and that the fool denies the God he knows.

17717.title: Who shall abide: separated unto His gospel
17717.summary: The Christian life is separation: no backbiting or evil to neighbours, condemning vile persons, keeping vows, avoiding usury and being doers of the word.

17721.title: Their drink offerings of blood: the Mass refuted
17721.summary: Roman Catholic drink offerings and repeated sacrifice of the Mass are offerings to another god, while Christ's blood was offered once for all.

17725.title: Importunity and imprecatory prayer are Biblical
17725.summary: Persistent prayer and imprecatory prayer, as in the parable of the widow, are Biblical and powerful tools of faith, against teachers who say otherwise.

17726.title: Praying for judgment with a clean heart
17726.summary: Imprecatory prayer must include self-examination and willingness to be judged by God's word the same way we ask Him to judge others.

17727.title: I shall be satisfied when I awake with thy likeness
17727.summary: God keeps His children under His wing, and our satisfaction is in the resurrection when we shall see Christ and be like Him, whatever the wicked gain now.

17730.title: Who is a rock save our God
17730.summary: Psalm 18 shows who the Lord is, our rock and deliverer, and there is no other rock nor name but Jesus, who rewards those who trust Him and destroys the wicked.

17737.title: All creation is a parable
17737.summary: Creation is a parable that shows God's might and love, and believers, as new creatures, are meant to declare His glory to the heathen like the heavens do.

17741.title: Save, LORD: the name of Christ in Psalm 20
17741.summary: Psalm 20 is praise for salvation in the name of Christ Jesus, the one offering, whose soul was not left in hell.

17742.title: Some trust in chariots, but we in the name of the LORD
17742.summary: Trusting the Lord rather than wealth or strength makes us sure of deliverance in every battle because we first trusted Him for eternal security.

17746.title: Length of days forever, and the fire that devours
17746.summary: Those who call on the Lord are given eternal life forever, while the wicked who reject Him are swallowed up in His wrath and fire.

17752.title: Our fathers trusted in thee and were delivered
17752.summary: God's faithfulness to the fathers, written for our learning, assures our deliverance even when we feel abandoned.

17754.title: In the midst of the congregation will I praise thee
17754.summary: Trials are an opportunity to overcome by God's power and praise Him among the brethren, which cannot be done by forsaking the assembly.

17761.title: Goodness and mercy shall follow me now
17761.summary: Though it points to the marriage feast, Psalm 23 mainly speaks of the peace and provision believers have now, along with eternal life.

17772.title: They that wait on thee shall not be ashamed
17772.summary: Psalm 25 models trusting prayer: lifting our souls to God, confessing sin that may bring chastening, and waiting on Him, never ashamed.

17773.title: The Authorized English loses nothing
17773.summary: The Hebrew acrostic form may be lost in translation, but the King James loses nothing of the power and truth of God's word.

17777.title: Judge not means no hypocrisy, not no judgment
17777.summary: Judge not warns against hypocrisy, not right judgment; like David we ask God to judge us first, separate from false believers, and enter the congregation with a clean conscience.

17778.title: Submit to His judgment and go to church
17778.summary: Psalm 26 presupposes going to church; avoiding God's judgment leads to skipping church and backsliding, which brings harsher chastening.

17780.title: Whom shall I fear: boldness to win souls
17780.summary: Saved by the Lord we have nothing to fear from men, yet many Christians fear knocking doors while missionaries face prison, and slogans on t-shirts are no bold stand.

17788.title: Destroy the wicked, spare thine anointed
17788.summary: Amid constant news of the wicked prospering, we pray for their destruction and our protection from His wrath, with joy instead of fear.

17799.title: In His favour is life
17799.summary: God's anger is for a moment but His favour, grace through Christ, is life, and the purpose of our salvation is to sing His praise forever.

17804.title: I trusted in thee: let the wicked be ashamed
17804.summary: In grief and isolation we trust the Lord, who saves us despite our sin, while the wicked who deny Him will be silenced in unquenchable fire.

17805.title: The LORD preserveth the faithful
17805.summary: Like Elijah we may feel alone, but God has reserved His own and will preserve the faithful from the wicked.

17811.title: Thou art my hiding place
17811.summary: Those who have called on the Lord can rest assured they are saved and preserved, already forgiven, and should come willingly to walk in His ways.

17816.title: The priests stood, but Christ sat down
17816.summary: The priests had no seat because their sacrifices never took away sins, but Christ sat down at God's right hand after one sacrifice forever.

17827.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
17827.title: Sing skilfully with instruments and doctrine
17827.summary: Scripture commands singing with instruments in the congregation, songs full of doctrine, avoiding both carnal rock-concert worship and the removal of instruments.

17829.theme: The church is the Israel of God
17829.title: Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD
17829.summary: The blessing on the nation whose God is the Lord is open to any people who trust Him, for those in Christ are Abraham's seed, and Israel was chosen to be a light to the Gentiles.

17830.title: God is no respecter of persons
17830.summary: Jewish ethnic supremacy is wicked since God is no respecter of persons; He judges individuals by faith and nations by works and always offered His blessing to any who trusted Him.

17833.title: Many are the afflictions of the righteous
17833.summary: God's commandments are for our good and He provides for His own, yet the godly will suffer affliction that grows faith, and none who trust Him will be desolate.

17844.title: Love thy enemies, and leave vengeance to the Judge
17844.summary: We love and pray for enemies in their need, but we need not pray for their success in evil and may ask God to repay those who reward good with evil.

17845.title: Avoid bargaining with God, give Him the glory
17845.summary: We may persistently ask God's help and promise praise, but bargaining with our works gives us room to boast and shares the glory that is His alone.

17850.theme: Fear is a lack of faith
17850.title: Fret not: gratitude casts out anxiety
17850.summary: We are commanded not to fret or envy the wicked, and gratitude to God, which science now confirms calms fear, is the means God gives to not be anxious.

17858.title: Godly sorrow versus the sorrow of the world
17858.summary: Cain sorrowed over his punishment but never repented, while David's godly sorrow hated his sin and worked repentance.

17863.title: I will keep my mouth with a bridle
17863.summary: Like David and James we bridle the tongue, sometimes keeping silent rather than speak in anger, and remember man's life is a handbreadth compared to the glory to come.

17871.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
17871.title: Praise, thanksgiving, confession, deliverance
17871.summary: We cannot acknowledge salvation without acknowledging the sin we are saved from, and David's psalm models praise, confession, deliverance and judgment in prayer.

17875.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
17875.title: Begin with confession: a warning to prayer warriors
17875.summary: Effective prayer reminds God of His promises and begins with honest confession, guarding prayer warriors against creeping pride.

17883.title: Why art thou cast down, O my soul
17883.summary: Remembering past deliverance does not automatically cure depression; it is fine to ask God why, without beating ourselves up, as long as we do not forget Him.

17890.title: Hope thou in God: the poor in spirit lifted up
17890.summary: Psalm 43, rightly kept separate in the KJV, shifts from lament to certain hope, showing God lifts up the poor in spirit, not only the super-faithful.

17922.title: Our fathers have told us: teaching children God's works
17922.summary: Fathers are commanded to tell their children what God has done, and remembering past deliverances with thanksgiving gives weight to prayer for present help.

17923.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
17923.title: Pre-trib wishful thinking and the persecuted saints
17923.summary: Christians have always suffered persecution and will under the beast; boastful post-trib posturing and pre-trib wishful thinking both look down on the suffering saints while living like the world.

17926.title: Counted as sheep for the slaughter, yet faithful
17926.summary: Psalm 44 shows the faithful, who cannot apostatize, can suffer without being punished for sin, and Paul uses it to show God eventually delivers His people.

17949.title: God is our refuge and strength
17949.summary: Throughout the Bible God is our refuge, and the gospel itself is His promise of protection and life kept in Christ.

17992.title: Call upon me in the day of trouble
17992.summary: God's call to call upon Him in trouble is the gospel to all men, and believers let their light shine so men glorify God.

17996.title: Professors who bury the talent
17996.summary: God's indictment in Psalm 50 is against false professors who bury His gift and think formal worship spares them from wrath, while His righteous are protected.

17997.title: Whited tombs: church as a checkbox
17997.summary: Those who treat church and ritual as proof of holiness are whited tombs; we assemble to exhort one another and stay salty, praising God until Christ comes.

18012.title: Against thee only have I sinned
18012.summary: David confesses his sin against God and owns that God's judgment is right, while those who resent God's judgment are destroyed by bitterness.

18013.title: I shall go to him: babies are not born condemned
18013.summary: David's words about going to his dead child show he did not believe babies are born guilty and condemned, refuting the doctrine of original sin built on Psalm 51:5.

18022.title: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation
18022.summary: David was not afraid of losing salvation but sought restored joy; God runs to the returning prodigal and wants a broken and contrite heart, not penance.
